docs.title: create_tutorial_flow()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def create_tutorial_flow() -> Flow:

Description: Constructs, configures, and returns the executable PocketFlow.Flow instance containing the full codebase documentation pipeline. The function manages the instantiation of all underlying execution nodes from nodes.py, configures fault-tolerant retry parameters across inference-backed stages, links execution dependencies via operator overloading (>> and -), logs graph generation telemetry via output.py, and designates FetchRepo as the root entry point.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * Flow: A fully wired PocketFlow.Flow execution graph initialized with FetchRepo as the starting node (start=fetch_repo).

Raises: * This function does not raise runtime exceptions directly during construction; graph validation or node initialization errors are delegated to the underlying pocketflow library or node constructors.

Implementation Phases:

docs.title: Node Instantiation and Parameter Configuration
docs.text:
fetch_repo = FetchRepo()
    context_router = ContextRouter()
    map_abstractions = MapAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    reduce_abstractions = ReduceAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    identify_abstractions = IdentifyAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    analyze_relationships = AnalyzeRelationships(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    order_chapters = OrderChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    write_chapters = WriteChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    combine_tutorial = CombineTutorial()
    deterministic_mapper = DeterministicFileMapper(max_retries=5, wait=20)

During this initial phase, the function instantiates ten node objects. Distinct operational requirements are reflected in their initialization arguments: purely deterministic or filesystem-bound nodes (FetchRepo, ContextRouter, and CombineTutorial) are instantiated with default retry parameters because their execution relies on deterministic local logic or terminal disk I/O. Conversely, all nodes interfacing with remote LLM provider APIs (MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions, IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters, WriteChapters, and DeterministicFileMapper) are explicitly injected with max_retries=5 and wait=20. This ensures that downstream transient network anomalies, remote provider HTTP 429 rate limits, and JSON/YAML deserialization issues are retried with 20-second backoffs before failing the flow.

docs.title: Graph Topology and Routing Definition
docs.text:
fetch_repo >> context_router

    context_router - "direct" >> identify_abstractions
    context_router - "batch" >> map_abstractions
    context_router - "deterministic" >> deterministic_mapper

    map_abstractions >> reduce_abstractions

    identify_abstractions >> analyze_relationships
    reduce_abstractions >> analyze_relationships

    analyze_relationships >> order_chapters
    order_chapters >> write_chapters

    deterministic_mapper >> write_chapters

    write_chapters >> combine_tutorial

This phase uses PocketFlow domain-specific operators to wire the pipeline's execution topology. Unconditional sequential steps are defined using the shift operator (>>), such that fetch_repo >> context_router ensures filesystem harvesting completes before evaluation starts. The conditional branching operator (- action >> target) splits execution from ContextRouter along three discrete paths based on repository size and mode ("direct", "batch", and "deterministic"). The graph then reconverges: both the "direct" and "batch" pipelines merge at AnalyzeRelationships, flow through OrderChapters, and reach WriteChapters. Concurrently, the "deterministic" path bypasses structural analysis entirely and links directly from DeterministicFileMapper to WriteChapters. Finally, chapter authoring unconditionally transitions to CombineTutorial for final site and file compilation.

docs.title: Telemetry Logging and Flow Encapsulation
docs.text:
emit_raw("DEBUG", "create_tutorial_flow | constructed PocketFlow execution graph", dest="LOG")
    return Flow(start=fetch_repo)

The final phase logs the graph creation event directly to disk logs using emit_raw() from utils/output.py. The call routes to dest="LOG" to prevent diagnostic noise from polluting standard interactive console streams. Once logged, the function wraps the complete execution topology into a pocketflow.Flow instance by binding fetch_repo as the designated root node, returning the flow object for downstream execution by main.py.

Example: 

# Call site extracted from main.py:
from flow import create_tutorial_flow

# ...
flow = create_tutorial_flow()
shared_context = {
    "repo_path": repo_path,
    # ... runtime parameters
}
flow.run(shared_context)

docs.title: Data Structures
docs.text: The flow.py module defines the structural integration between the underlying PocketFlow engine and the node implementations in nodes.py. It operates over the following structural contracts:

docs.title: Pipeline Node Execution Profiles
docs.text:
The nodes instantiated within flow.py adhere to specific configuration profiles depending on whether they perform deterministic operations or remote inference:

Node Variable Target Node Class Execution Category Configured Retries (max_retries) Backoff (wait) Upstream Dependencies Downstream Targets fetch_repo FetchRepo Deterministic I/O Default (0) Default (0) None (Start Node) context_router context_router ContextRouter Evaluation / Routing Default (0) Default (0) fetch_repo identify_abstractions, map_abstractions, deterministic_mapper identify_abstractions IdentifyAbstractions LLM Inference 5 20s context_router ("direct") analyze_relationships map_abstractions MapAbstractions LLM Inference 5 20s context_router ("batch") reduce_abstractions reduce_abstractions ReduceAbstractions LLM Inference 5 20s map_abstractions analyze_relationships deterministic_mapper DeterministicFileMapper LLM / Fallback 5 20s context_router ("deterministic") write_chapters analyze_relationships AnalyzeRelationships LLM Inference 5 20s identify_abstractions, reduce_abstractions order_chapters order_chapters OrderChapters LLM Inference 5 20s analyze_relationships write_chapters write_chapters WriteChapters LLM Inference 5 20s order_chapters, deterministic_mapper combine_tutorial combine_tutorial CombineTutorial Deterministic I/O Default (0) Default (0) write_chapters None (End Node)

docs.title: Branch Action Routing Contract
docs.text:
The context_router node outputs string action tokens that determine edge traversal across the conditional branches:

Action Identifier Trigger Condition Activated Node Skipped Subgraphs "direct" Single-prompt codebase token size below context ceiling. IdentifyAbstractions map_abstractions, reduce_abstractions, deterministic_mapper "batch" Large codebase token size exceeding context ceiling; requires batching. MapAbstractions identify_abstractions, deterministic_mapper "deterministic" Operational mode specifies 1:1 file-to-chapter documentation. DeterministicFileMapper identify_abstractions, map_abstractions, reduce_abstractions, analyze_relationships, order_chapters

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The flow.py file delegates runtime exception handling to PocketFlow and the internal retry logic of individual nodes. However, it implements proactive fault tolerance through constructor parameter injection:

  • Inference Rate Limiting & Transient Flakiness: All nodes interacting with external LLMs (map_abstractions, reduce_abstractions, identify_abstractions, analyze_relationships, order_chapters, write_chapters, and deterministic_mapper) are configured with max_retries=5 and wait=20. When an underlying node encounters an API error, rate limit (HTTP 429), or malformed response format, PocketFlow intercepts the failure and sleeps for 20 seconds before retrying the node's prep -> exec -> post cycle, up to 5 times.
  • Deterministic Isolation: Nodes executing deterministic operations (FetchRepo, ContextRouter, and CombineTutorial) omit max_retries and wait. Failures within these stages (e.g., repository path not found, disk full, or write permission denied) are treated as fatal configuration or environmental errors and bubble up immediately to main.py without delaying the user with redundant retry cycles.

docs.title: main.py
docs.text:
Source: main.py

As established in the system hierarchy, flow.py defines the declarative Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) that coordinates repository ingestion, abstraction mapping, relationship extraction, chapter ordering, and documentation synthesis. main.py serves as the primary application bootstrapper, command-line interface (CLI) driver, and runtime lifecycle controller for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder platform. It bridges human operator intent, operating system environment variables, filesystem state, and remote provider credentials into the execution context consumed by the underlying computational graph.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
main.py functions as the centralized operational orchestrator responsible for validating runtime invariants, resolving complex configuration matrices, and executing the documentation pipeline. It begins execution by loading .env configuration files via dotenv.load_dotenv() and establishing terminal argument parsing. The module performs multi-tier input sanitization—detecting accidental shell glob swallows, reconciling legacy execution flags, verifying remote Large Language Model (LLM) authentication credentials prior to network-heavy crawling, and compiling per-node reasoning plans using provider-specific heuristics.

At the core of its operational lifecycle, main.py constructs the canonical shared state store dictionary. This state dictionary acts as the persistent blackboard across all workflow graph nodes instantiated by flow.py. During the run, main.py configures disk logging, resolves model context ceilings, outputs diagnostic preflight summaries, initializes string localization engines, and hands execution control to the PocketFlow engine. The execution phase is wrapped within an isolated try...finally block, ensuring that comprehensive token ledger accounting, cumulative provider expenditures, and process resource teardown are performed even if an unhandled exception or terminal refusal occurs deep within pipeline inference stages.

flowchart TD
    subgraph Preflight["Preflight Initialization & Validation"]
        startNode["parse_arguments()"] --> checkQuotes{"_check_quoting_errors()"}
        checkQuotes --> resolvePlan["resolve_thinking_plan()"]
        resolvePlan --> initOut["init_output(auto_translate=False)"]
        initOut --> valPlan{"_validate_thinking_args()"}
        valPlan --> cleanupCheck{"args.cleanup (standalone)?"}
        cleanupCheck -- "Yes" --> runCleanup["_run_cleanup()"] --> exitEarly["sys.exit(0)"]
        cleanupCheck -- "No" --> checkTarget{"--repo or --dir provided?"}
        checkTarget -- "No" --> throwErr["parser.error()"]
        checkTarget -- "Yes" --> checkAuth{"check_llm_auth()"}
        checkAuth -- "Fail" --> exitAuth["sys.exit(1)"]

Description: Configures and executes the complete CLI parsing schema for the application using Python's standard argparse module. docs.title: Phase 1: Source and Cleanup Argument Grouping
docs.text:
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate a tutorial for a GitHub codebase or local directory.")

    # Source: --repo or --dir (mutually exclusive but not required if --cleanup is used)
    source_group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    source_group.add_argument("--repo", help="URL of the public GitHub repository.")
    source_group.add_argument("--dir", help="Path to local directory.")
    parser.add_argument("--cleanup", action="store_true", help="Clean up logs and cache files. Can be used standalone or after a run.")

    parser.add_argument("-n", "--name", help="Project name (optional, derived from repo/directory if omitted).")
    parser.add_argument("-t", "--token", help="GitHub personal access token (optional, reads from GITHUB_TOKEN env var if not provided).")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", default="output", help="Base directory for output (default: ./output).")
    parser.add_argument("-i", "--include", nargs="+", help="Files to include (e.g., '*.py' '*.js'). Defaults to '*' (all files).")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-e",
        "--exclude",
        nargs="+",
        help="Files to exclude. Custom patterns are automatically merged with a massive global exclusion list (build caches, node_modules, binaries, media, AI environments) AND your repository's native .gitignore rules.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("-s", "--max-size", type=int, default=200000, help="Maximum file size in bytes (default: 200000, about 200KB).")
This initial phase establishes the mutually exclusive ingestion target parameter group ensuring that an operator cannot specify both a remote GitHub URL and a local directory simultaneously. It configures default filesystem targets, including an output destination defaulting to ./output and a conservative default file size boundary of 200,000 bytes (approximately 200 KB) to defend memory buffers against multi-megabyte binary dumps. File pattern arguments are defined as multi-value lists via nargs="+", allowing operators to pass arbitrary space-separated globs that downstream crawling components merge with defaults.

docs.title: resolve_mode_and_project()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_mode_and_project(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[str, str]:

Description: Reconciles generation mode options and derives a normalized project identifier. It handles backward-compatibility logic for the legacy --advanced boolean flag, emitting a warning if both --mode and --advanced were specified concurrently. If an explicit project name was not supplied via -n/--name, it derives a deterministic name by inspecting filesystem base paths or stripping .git extensions from repository URLs.

def resolve_mode_and_project(args):
    """Resolve documentation mode (handling --advanced legacy flag) and derive project name.

    Returns:
        tuple[str, str]: (mode, project_name)
    """
    if args.advanced:
        if args.mode != "tutorial":  # User explicitly set --mode AND --advanced
            emit("WARN_ADVANCED_OVERRIDES_MODE", mode=args.mode)
        mode = "advanced"
    else:
        mode = args.mode
    project_name = args.name
    if not project_name:
        if args.dir:
            project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(args.dir))
        elif args.repo:
            project_name = args.repo.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1].removesuffix(".git")
        else:
            project_name = "project"
    return mode, project_name
The implementation uses defensive fallback resolution. When inspecting local directory paths, os.path.abspath normalizes relative markers (. or ..) before os.path.basename isolates the directory name. When evaluating remote repository URLs, trailing slashes are stripped via rstrip("/"), the terminal URI component is isolated via split("/")[-1], and .git suffixes are removed via removesuffix(".git"). If neither --dir nor --repo can yield a name (e.g., in edge cases or standalone cleanup runs), it falls back to the literal string "project".

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed command-line argument container.

Returns: * tuple[str, str]: A 2-tuple where the first element is the normalized documentation mode ("tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", or "sdk"), and the second element is the resolved project name string.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

mode, project_name = resolve_mode_and_project(args)

docs.title: build_shared_store()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_shared_store(args: argparse.Namespace, github_token: str | None, mode: str, thinking_plan: dict[str, str | None], project_name: str) -> dict[str, any]:

Description: Constructs the canonical shared state blackboard dictionary that is passed into PocketFlow.Flow.run() and mutated across all downstream workflow nodes. It centralizes operational limits, glob sets, reasoning allocations, credentials, and pre-allocated output slots.

def build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name):
    """Construct the shared store dictionary passed between PocketFlow nodes.

    Returns:
        dict: The shared store with all CLI args, patterns, and empty output slots.
    """
    return {
        "repo_url": args.repo,
        "local_dir": args.dir,
        "project_name": project_name,  # Resolved once in main so logs, --force-rebuild and output agree
        "github_token": github_token,
        "output_dir": args.output,  # Base directory for CombineTutorial output
        # Include/exclude patterns and max file size
        "include_patterns": set(args.include) if args.include else DEFAULT_INCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "exclude_patterns": DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS.union(set(args.exclude)) if args.exclude else DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "max_file_size": args.max_size,
        # Language for multi-language support
        "language": args.language,
        # Cache flag (inverse of no-cache)
        "use_cache": not args.no_cache,
        # Max abstractions
        "max_abstraction_num": args.max_abstractions,
        # LLM reasoning capabilities: global level (legacy) + per-node plan (utils/thinking.py)
        "thinking_level": args.thinking_level,
        "thinking_plan": thinking_plan,
        # Max tokens override
        "max_tokens": args.max_tokens,
        # Mode, mkdocs, and incremental
        "mode": mode,
        "mkdocs": args.mkdocs,
        "incremental": args.incremental,
        "advanced_mode": mode == "advanced",
        # Batching settings
        "batch_size": args.batch,
        "force_batch": args.force_batch,
        # Debug mode
        "debug": args.debug,
        # Outputs populated by downstream nodes
        "files": [],
        "abstractions": [],
        "relationships": {},
        "chapter_order": [],
        "chapters": [],
        "final_output_dir": None,
    }
This function merges user-specified exclusion patterns directly with the module constant DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS imported from utils/exclude_patterns.py using set union operations. If no custom inclusion list was provided, it falls back to DEFAULT_INCLUDE_PATTERNS ({"*"}). Crucially, it sets up empty data structures (files, abstractions, relationships, chapter_order, chapters) that nodes in nodes.py incrementally populate during execution, ensuring that missing dictionary key exceptions do not occur.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Deserialized CLI argument attributes. * github_token (str | None): Authenticated personal access token for GitHub API interactions, or None. * mode (str): Resolved operational mode ("tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", or "sdk"). * thinking_plan (dict[str, str | None]): Mapping of node identification keys to resolved reasoning levels. * project_name (str): Derived project identifier string.

Returns: * dict[str, any]: Comprehensive state dictionary serving as the pipeline execution context.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

shared = build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name)

docs.title: detect_llm_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def detect_llm_config(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[str, str, str, str, int]:

Description: Inspects the operational environment to identify the active LLM provider, target model name, network endpoint URL, API authorization key, and context window ceiling. It defers import of get_model_context_length from utils/llm_config.py to avoid unnecessary overhead during non-generation executions (e.g. --cleanup).

def detect_llm_config(args):
    """Detect LLM provider, model, endpoint, and context length from environment.

    Returns:
        tuple: (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length)
    """
    from utils.llm_config import get_model_context_length

    provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key = resolve_llm_settings()
    context_length = args.max_tokens or get_model_context_length(endpoint_url, model_name, api_key)
    return provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length
The function delegates base credential and endpoint resolution to resolve_llm_settings(). To determine the effective context length, it applies a prioritized fallback check: if the operator supplied an explicit --max-tokens integer via the CLI, that value overrides all dynamic determinations; otherwise, get_model_context_length() dynamically inspects the remote provider or internal capability catalogs to return the ceiling.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI options containing the optional max_tokens override.

Returns: * tuple[str, str, str, str, int]: A 5-tuple structured as (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length).

Raises: * None. (Underlying resolution errors are trapped upstream or within resolve_llm_settings).

Example: 

provider, model_name, endpoint_url, _, context_length = detect_llm_config(args)

docs.title: resolve_thinking_plan()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_thinking_plan(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[str, dict[str, str | None], list[str]]:

Description: Compiles the granular per-node reasoning effort plan based on operator CLI flags (--thinking-override, --thinking-level, --thinking-profile). It executes prior to output telemetry initialization and contains no emit() logging side-effects, making it a pure configuration resolution step.

def resolve_thinking_plan(args):
    """Build the per-node thinking plan from --thinking-override / --thinking-level / --thinking-profile.

    Pure (no emit): runs before init_output(). Validation messages come from _validate_thinking_args().

    Returns:
        tuple[str, dict, list[str]]: (resolved profile name, {node_key: level | None}, invalid override strings)
    """
    mode = "advanced" if args.advanced else args.mode
    overrides, invalid = parse_overrides(args.thinking_override)
    profile = "global" if args.thinking_level else resolve_profile_name(args.thinking_profile, resolve_llm_settings()[0])
    return profile, build_thinking_plan(profile, mode, args.thinking_level, overrides), invalid
The implementation first parses raw key-value override strings into structured dictionaries and invalid token lists via parse_overrides() from utils/thinking.py. If a global --thinking-level was requested, the profile identifier is categorized as "global"; otherwise, resolve_profile_name() maps the requested profile (e.g., "auto", "balanced") against the active provider detected by resolve_llm_settings()[0]. Finally, build_thinking_plan() computes the final dictionary mapping each node key to an effort tier or None.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): CLI namespace containing thinking arguments.

Returns: * tuple[str, dict[str, str | None], list[str]]: A 3-tuple containing: 1. The resolved profile name string (profile). 2. The resolved per-node thinking plan dictionary ({node_key: level | None}). 3. A list of unparseable or malformed override strings (invalid).

Raises: * None.

Example: 

thinking_profile, thinking_plan, invalid_overrides = resolve_thinking_plan(args)

docs.title: display_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def display_config(args: argparse.Namespace, mode: str, provider: str, model_name: str, endpoint_url: str, context_length: int, log_file: str, thinking_profile: str, thinking_plan: dict[str, str | None]) -> None:

Description: Broadcasts the resolved runtime execution configuration, model parameters, cognitive reasoning plans, batch thresholds, and storage paths to the console via the localized emission bus in utils/output.py.

def display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan):
    """Emit all configuration values to the console."""
    emit("START_GENERATION", source=args.repo or args.dir, language=args.language.capitalize())
    emit("CFG_HEADER")
    emit("CFG_AI_PROVIDER", value=provider)
    emit("CFG_AI_ENDPOINT", value=endpoint_url)
    emit("CFG_AI_MODEL", value=model_name)
    emit("CFG_CONTEXT_LENGTH", value=f"{context_length:,}")
    emit("CFG_THINKING_LEVEL", value=args.thinking_level or "None")
    emit("CFG_THINKING_PROFILE", value=thinking_profile)
    if any(thinking_plan.values()):
        emit("CFG_THINKING_PLAN", value=describe_plan(thinking_plan, mode))
    emit("CFG_THINKING_SUPPORT", value=describe_thinking_support(provider, model_name))
    emit("CFG_TOKEN_RATIO", value=describe_token_ratio())
    emit("CFG_BATCH_SIZE", value=f"{args.batch}")
    _enabled = get("CFG_VALUE_ENABLED")
    _disabled = get("CFG_VALUE_DISABLED")
    emit("CFG_FORCE_BATCH", value=_enabled if args.force_batch else _disabled)
    emit("CFG_OUTPUT_MODE", value=mode)
    emit("CFG_MKDOCS", value=_enabled if args.mkdocs else _disabled)
    emit("CFG_INCREMENTAL", value=_enabled if args.incremental else _disabled)
    if args.incremental:
        emit("CFG_FORCE_REBUILD", value=_enabled if args.force_rebuild else _disabled)
    if mode == "api-reference":
        emit("CFG_MAX_ABSTRACTIONS", value=get("CFG_VALUE_API_REF_MAX"))
    else:
        emit("CFG_MAX_ABSTRACTIONS", value=str(args.max_abstractions))
    emit("CFG_LLM_CACHING", value=_disabled if args.no_cache else _enabled)
    if args.debug:
        emit("CFG_DEBUG_MODE")
    emit("CFG_LOG_FILE", value=log_file)
    print()  # Blank line after config block
This function transforms internal runtime states into human-readable console banners using translatable template keys defined in strings.csv. It retrieves localized representations of boolean states (CFG_VALUE_ENABLED vs CFG_VALUE_DISABLED) via get(), queries utils/thinking.py to render a formatted plan breakdown via describe_plan(), queries utils/token_utils.py for dynamic tokenizer ratio diagnostics via describe_token_ratio(), and prints the persistent log file path.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Deserialized CLI argument state. * mode (str): Resolved documentation mode string. * provider (str): Detected LLM provider name. * model_name (str): Sanitized model identifier string. * endpoint_url (str): Transport endpoint URL for API requests. * context_length (int): Active context window size in tokens. * log_file (str): Resolved filesystem path to the active timestamped log file. * thinking_profile (str): Active reasoning profile name. * thinking_plan (dict[str, str | None]): Complete per-node reasoning level map.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan)

docs.title: main()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def main() -> None:

Description: The primary entry-point orchestrator executing the full lifecycle of the application. It parses arguments, validates flags and credentials, handles caching, initializes telemetry, builds the shared state blackboard, executes the graph flow, and enforces cleanup and cost reporting in a finally block.

docs.title: Phase 1: Pre-Execution Validation and Output Bootstrapping
docs.text:
def main():
    parser, args = parse_arguments()
    # Resolved silently before init_output(): string translation itself uses the plan's translate_strings level.
    thinking_profile, thinking_plan, invalid_overrides = resolve_thinking_plan(args)
    # Translation of missing strings is an LLM call: deferred until arguments and credentials are checked.
    init_output(
        language=args.language,
        use_cache=not args.no_cache,
        thinking_level=thinking_plan["translate_strings"],
        debug=args.debug,
        auto_translate=False,
    )
    _check_quoting_errors(parser, args)
    _validate_thinking_args(args, invalid_overrides)

    # Handle standalone --cleanup (no --dir or --repo)
    if args.cleanup and not args.dir and not args.repo:
        _run_cleanup()
        return

    # Require --dir or --repo for generation
    if not args.dir and not args.repo:
        parser.error("one of the arguments --repo --dir --cleanup is required")
This phase bootstraps the environment while guarding against configuration flaws. Thinking plans are resolved before telemetry initialization so that the localized translation subsystem can inherit its configured thinking level. Calling init_output() configures stream encodings and initializes in-memory telemetry buffers while deliberately deferring LLM string translation (auto_translate=False). Defensive validators immediately inspect arguments for shell quoting errors or conflicting thinking overrides. If the standalone --cleanup flag was passed without an ingestion target, cleanup is executed immediately and the process terminates gracefully.

docs.title: Phase 2: LLM Preflight Authentication and Cache Sanitization
docs.text:
# Fail fast (with setup instructions) before crawling if the configured provider cannot authenticate
    if not check_llm_auth():
        sys.exit(1)
    translate_missing_strings()
    notice_legacy_cache()

    # Get GitHub token from argument or environment variable if using repo
    github_token = None
    if args.repo:
        github_token = args.token or os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN")
        if not github_token:
            emit("WARN_NO_GITHUB_TOKEN")
    elif args.token:
        emit("WARN_TOKEN_NO_REPO")

    mode, project_name = resolve_mode_and_project(args)

    # Enforce incremental cache constraints
    if args.incremental and mode != "api-reference":
        emit("WARN_INCREMENTAL_API_ONLY")
        args.incremental = False

    # --force-rebuild requires --incremental
    if args.force_rebuild and not args.incremental:
        emit("ERROR_FORCE_REBUILD_NO_INCREMENTAL")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Handle --force-rebuild: delete the cache manifest to force fresh generation
    if args.force_rebuild and args.incremental:
        output_base = args.output or "output"
        manifest_path = os.path.join(output_base, project_name, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
        if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
            os.remove(manifest_path)
            emit("FORCE_REBUILD_DELETED", path=manifest_path)
        else:
            emit("FORCE_REBUILD_NO_MANIFEST", path=manifest_path)

    # Warn about args ignored in api-reference mode
    if mode == "api-reference" and args.force_batch:
        emit("WARN_FORCE_BATCH_API_REF")
        args.force_batch = False
This phase enforces preflight checks. It calls check_llm_auth() from utils/llm_config.py to fail fast if API credentials are invalid or absent, preventing unnecessary local or remote repository crawling. Once credentials pass verification, missing localization strings are translated via translate_missing_strings(), and legacy cache files are migrated or reported via notice_legacy_cache(). GitHub personal access tokens are resolved from CLI flags or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variables. Mode-specific constraints are then validated: incremental generation is strictly gated to api-reference mode, and --force-rebuild deletes the .doc_cache_manifest.json file on disk to guarantee a cold run.

docs.title: Phase 3: Flow Execution and Guaranteed Lifecycle Teardown
docs.text:
shared = build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name)
    provider, model_name, endpoint_url, _, context_length = detect_llm_config(args)
    log_file = configure_logging(project_name=project_name, mode=mode)
    display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan)

    # Create and run the flow
    tutorial_flow = create_tutorial_flow()
    try:
        tutorial_flow.run(shared)

        # Cleanup after run if requested
        if args.cleanup:
            _run_cleanup()
    finally:
        from utils.output import shutdown

        # Report spend even when the run fails — failed runs are often the expensive ones.
        try:
            _emit_usage_summary()
        except Exception as e:
            emit_raw("WARNING", f"Usage summary failed: {e}", dest="LOG")
        shutdown()
In the final phase, build_shared_store() constructs the runtime state blackboard, persistent file logging is initialized via configure_logging(), and runtime configurations are displayed to the console. create_tutorial_flow() from flow.py compiles the DAG, and tutorial_flow.run(shared) launches execution. The pipeline is wrapped in a try...finally block to guarantee lifecycle teardown: whether the run succeeds, is aborted, or fails due to an API refusal, _emit_usage_summary() aggregates and prints total token expenditures and estimated USD costs before shutdown() flushes and closes active log file handles.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * SystemExit: If authentication checks fail, argument validation fails, or terminal configuration errors occur.

Example:

docs.title: _thinking_level_arg()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _thinking_level_arg(value: str) -> str | None:

Description: Custom validator and type converter callback for argparse processing the --thinking-level parameter. It strips surrounding whitespace, normalizes inputs to lowercase, maps empty strings or the literal token "default" to Python's None (representing the upstream model's default reasoning level), and validates explicit tiers against THINKING_LEVELS.

def _thinking_level_arg(value):
    """argparse type for --thinking-level: a level from THINKING_LEVELS; '' or 'default' → None (model default)."""
    level = value.strip().lower()
    if level in ("", "default"):
        return None
    if level not in THINKING_LEVELS:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"invalid choice: {value!r} (choose from {', '.join(THINKING_LEVELS)}, default)")
    return level
This helper enforces strict typing within the argparse layer rather than deferring validation to downstream execution nodes. By checking against THINKING_LEVELS (imported from utils/thinking.py), it intercepts invalid reasoning inputs early during initial CLI parsing. If an operator supplies an unrecognized string, it raises an argparse.ArgumentTypeError containing a list of permitted values, causing the parser to exit immediately with standard usage instructions.

Parameters: * value (str): The raw string passed on the command line for --thinking-level.

Returns: * str | None: A validated string level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high", "max") or None if the operator indicated the model default.

Raises: * argparse.ArgumentTypeError: If value is neither empty, "default", nor contained in THINKING_LEVELS.

Example: 

parser.add_argument(
    "--thinking-level",
    default=None,
    type=_thinking_level_arg,
    metavar="{" + ",".join(THINKING_LEVELS) + "}",
    help="Global thinking effort for EVERY LLM call.",
)

docs.title: _check_quoting_errors()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _check_quoting_errors(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser, args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:

Description: Inspects multi-argument pattern lists for accidental shell glob swallowing. When users omit or misquote nested quotes in shell terminals (e.g. --exclude "dir/* "other/*" --language ja), the command-line shell can merge subsequent CLI flags directly into pattern values. This causes following arguments to be silently swallowed as file patterns. This function detects such occurrences dynamically by checking whether any pattern contains a registered CLI flag.

def _check_quoting_errors(parser, args):
    """Detect shell quoting errors where --exclude/--include values accidentally swallowed other CLI flags.

    When users misquote patterns (e.g., --exclude "autogen/* "SmartFO/*" --language Vietnamese),
    the shell merges subsequent flags into the pattern value. This silently causes ALL following
    arguments to be ignored. We detect this by checking if any pattern value contains a known
    CLI flag string, which no legitimate file/directory pattern would ever contain.

    Flags are extracted dynamically from the argparse parser — no hardcoded list to maintain.
    """
    # Extract all registered flags (both --long and -short) from the parser
    known_flags = set()
    for action in parser._actions:
        for opt in action.option_strings:
            known_flags.add(opt)

    for pattern_list, flag_name in [(args.exclude, "--exclude"), (args.include, "--include")]:
        if not pattern_list:
            continue
        for pattern in pattern_list:
            for known_flag in known_flags:
                if f" {known_flag} " in pattern or (f" {known_flag}" in pattern and pattern.endswith(known_flag)):
                    emit(
                        "ERROR_QUOTING",
                        flag=flag_name,
                        pattern=pattern[:120],
                        embedded=known_flag,
                    )
                    sys.exit(1)
The helper inspects all actions registered within the active ArgumentParser instance (parser._actions), compiling a set of known option strings (known_flags, including both short flags like -o and long flags like --output). It then iterates across elements in args.exclude and args.include. If an element contains an embedded flag token delimited by spaces or located at the end of the string, it emits an ERROR_QUOTING diagnostic and immediately terminates the process via sys.exit(1).

Parameters: * parser (argparse.ArgumentParser): The active argument parser containing registered option strings. * args (argparse.Namespace): Deserialized CLI options to inspect.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * SystemExit: Raised with code 1 if a quoting violation is detected.

Example: 

_check_quoting_errors(parser, args)

docs.title: _validate_thinking_args()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _validate_thinking_args(args: argparse.Namespace, invalid_overrides: list[str]) -> None:

Description: Validates reasoning arguments against operational mode constraints. It halts the process if malformed override tokens were supplied, issues warnings if overrides target nodes that the active documentation mode does not execute, and warns operators if a global --thinking-level overrides an explicit --thinking-profile.

def _validate_thinking_args(args, invalid_overrides):
    """Report malformed --thinking-override values (fatal), overrides for nodes the mode never runs,
    and --thinking-level/--thinking-profile conflicts."""
    if invalid_overrides:
        emit("ERROR_THINKING_OVERRIDE", value=", ".join(invalid_overrides), nodes=", ".join(NODE_KEYS), levels=", ".join(THINKING_LEVELS))
        sys.exit(1)
    mode = "advanced" if args.advanced else args.mode
    overrides, _ = parse_overrides(args.thinking_override)
    unused = [node for node in overrides if node not in MODE_NODES[mode]]
    if unused:
        emit("WARN_THINKING_OVERRIDE_UNUSED", nodes=", ".join(unused), mode=mode, active=", ".join(MODE_NODES[mode]))
    if args.thinking_level and args.thinking_profile != "auto":
        emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_OVERRIDES_PROFILE", level=args.thinking_level, profile=args.thinking_profile)
This validation helper coordinates with mappings in utils/thinking.py. If invalid_overrides contains unparseable entries, it emits ERROR_THINKING_OVERRIDE (listing valid node identifiers and levels) and halts execution. It then checks active overrides against MODE_NODES[mode]. For instance, if an operator passes write_chapters=high while running --mode api-reference (which relies on deterministic_file_mapper instead), it issues WARN_THINKING_OVERRIDE_UNUSED. Finally, it identifies conflicting configurations when an explicit profile was specified alongside a monolithic --thinking-level.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): CLI options container. * invalid_overrides (list[str]): List of malformed NODE=LEVEL override strings returned by resolve_thinking_plan().

Returns: * None.

Raises: * SystemExit: Raised with exit code 1 if invalid_overrides is non-empty.

Example: 

_validate_thinking_args(args, invalid_overrides)

docs.title: _run_cleanup()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _run_cleanup() -> None:

Description: Deletes local disk caches, temporary staging files, token ratio calibration files, and persistent execution log directories.

def _run_cleanup():
    """Clean up cache files and log directory."""
    emit("CLEANUP_START")

    for cache_path in [cache_file, f"{cache_file}.tmp", LEGACY_CACHE_FILE, TOKEN_CALIBRATION_FILE, f"{TOKEN_CALIBRATION_FILE}.tmp"]:
        if os.path.exists(cache_path):
            try:
                os.remove(cache_path)
                emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED", path=cache_path)
            except Exception as e:
                emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=cache_path, error=e)

    log_dir = os.environ.get("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    if os.path.exists(log_dir) and os.path.isdir(log_dir):
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(log_dir)
            emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED_DIR", path=log_dir)
        except Exception as e:
            emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=log_dir, error=e)
The cleanup routine executes an isolated filesystem sweep. It targets active prompt cache files (cache_file), temporary atomic write buffers (.tmp), legacy cache locations (LEGACY_CACHE_FILE imported from utils/call_llm.py), and calibration states (TOKEN_CALIBRATION_FILE from utils/token_utils.py). It then queries the LOG_DIR environment variable (defaulting to "logs") and recursively removes the directory using shutil.rmtree. Every deletion and potential I/O failure is wrapped in defensive try...except blocks and reported through localized emit() events.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * None. (All filesystem exceptions are caught and emitted).

Example: 

if args.cleanup and not args.dir and not args.repo:
    _run_cleanup()
    return

docs.title: _emit_usage_summary()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _emit_usage_summary() -> None:

Description: Aggregates and renders complete provider-level token ledgers, estimated USD operational costs, invocation counts, cache hit metrics, and individual pipeline step breakdowns upon workflow termination.

def _emit_usage_summary():
    """Emit accumulated token usage and estimated cost per provider, then the per-step breakdown."""
    from utils.llm_common import get_step_summary, get_usage_summary
    from utils.token_utils import emit_step_usage, format_cost

    for name, usage in get_usage_summary().items():
        emit(
            "LLM_USAGE_SUMMARY",
            provider=name,
            models=", ".join(usage["models"]) or "-",
            calls=f"{usage['calls']:,}",
            input=f"{usage['input']:,}",
            output=f"{usage['output']:,}",
            thinking=f"{usage['thinking']:,}",
            cache_read=f"{usage['cache_read']:,}",
            cache_write=f"{usage['cache_write']:,}",
            cost=format_cost(usage),
            refusals=usage["refusals"],
            fallbacks=usage["fallbacks"],
            truncations=usage["truncations"],
        )
    steps = get_step_summary()
    if steps:
        emit("LLM_USAGE_STEPS_HEADER")
        for step, usage in steps.items():
            emit_step_usage("LLM_USAGE_STEP", step, usage)
This reporting helper dynamically imports accounting functions from utils/llm_common.py and formatting utilities from utils/token_utils.py. It iterates over the dictionary returned by get_usage_summary(), formatting provider totals for input tokens, generation tokens, internal reasoning tokens, prompt caching metrics, provider refusals, fallback downgrades, and length truncations. If step-level context attribution was active during the workflow, it iterates over get_step_summary(), invoking emit_step_usage() to print a per-node token breakdown.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * None. (Exceptions during summary generation are caught by caller try...except wrappers).

Example: 

finally:
    from utils.output import shutdown
    try:
        _emit_usage_summary()
    except Exception as e:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Usage summary failed: {e}", dest="LOG")
    shutdown()

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
main.py applies defensive input validation, preflight authentication verification, and fail-safe lifecycle teardown to ensure reliability across execution phases:

  • Shell Quoting Error Detection: Misquoted arguments (e.g., missing closing quotes around glob patterns) can cause subsequent CLI flags to be swallowed as pattern values. The _check_quoting_errors() helper inspects all --include and --exclude inputs against all registered flags in parser._actions. If an embedded flag is detected, the program emits ERROR_QUOTING with diagnostic details and exits immediately with code 1.
  • Malformed Reasoning Overrides: The _validate_thinking_args() helper checks for invalid NODE=LEVEL pairs. If unparseable entries are found, it emits ERROR_THINKING_OVERRIDE (listing supported nodes and effort tiers) and terminates with code 1. It also issues non-fatal warnings for unused overrides or conflicting --thinking-level and --thinking-profile arguments.
  • Preflight Authentication Gate: Before initiating filesystem crawling or remote repository downloads, main() invokes check_llm_auth() from utils/llm_config.py. If required API keys or environment variables are missing or malformed, the check prints actionable setup instructions and main() terminates via sys.exit(1), avoiding failed runs after expensive clone operations.
  • Incremental Rebuild Constraints: Incremental caching is validated against the active documentation mode. If --incremental is specified for modes other than api-reference, the flag is disabled with a WARN_INCREMENTAL_API_ONLY warning. If --force-rebuild is supplied without --incremental, the program emits ERROR_FORCE_REBUILD_NO_INCREMENTAL and terminates with code 1.
  • Guaranteed Accounting and Resource Cleanup: The entire execution pipeline is wrapped in a try...finally block. Regardless of whether the flow completes successfully, is cancelled by the operator, or raises an unhandled exception (such as an unrecoverable LLMRefusalError), _emit_usage_summary() runs inside the finally block to report accumulated token expenditures, reasoning costs, and cache metrics before utils.output.shutdown() closes logging streams.

docs.title: nodes.py
docs.text:
Source: nodes.py

In the overall pipeline architecture, main.py bootstraps the runtime environment, validates provider credentials, and initializes the shared blackboard store before handing execution control over to the Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) constructed in flow.py. The nodes.py module implements the concrete computational units of this DAG, defining every discrete transformation, LLM reasoning step, batch-processing routine, and file-emission task as a subclass of pocketflow.Node or pocketflow.BatchNode.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
nodes.py serves as the primary operational execution layer for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. It bridges the gap between raw repository files and structured, multi-chapter technical documentation. The module consumes the blackboard dictionary initialized during bootstrapping, iteratively reading and mutating shared keys as execution progresses through repository ingestion, abstraction extraction, topological relationship modeling, narrative synthesis, and artifact publishing.

The module implements three architectural execution pathways dynamically selected based on operational mode and token capacity constraints. In the Direct Route, whole codebases fitting within model context windows are analyzed holistically to extract core abstractions. In the Batch Route, codebases exceeding single-context safety thresholds are partitioned into directory-isolated batches, mapped across parallel or sequential LLM invocations, and reduced into a unified abstraction hierarchy. In the Deterministic Route (used for api-reference mode), code files are filtered and mapped directly to internal API chapters one-to-one, bypassing abstraction extraction entirely.

Each node adheres to PocketFlow's three-phase execution contract: prep() validates inputs and builds prompts or batch items; exec() performs the primary computation or network I/O wrapped in standardized error-handling decorators; and post() unpacks results, mutates shared state, and determines graph routing transitions. Furthermore, the module embeds incremental disk caching, cross-chapter summary propagation, foundation-node topological highlighting, and dual-output format generation (MkDocs Material or standalone Markdown).

docs.title: FetchRepo.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> dict:

Description: Gathers repository ingestion configuration parameters from the shared dictionary. If project_name is missing, it dynamically derives a clean name from the trailing segment of the repository URL (stripping .git) or from the absolute directory path basename.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global workflow state dictionary containing configuration flags, repository sources, and inclusion/exclusion globs.

Returns: * dict: Ingestion parameter packet containing repo_url, local_dir, token, include_patterns, exclude_patterns, max_file_size, and use_relative_paths.

Example: 

# Extracted from FetchRepo.prep() implementation in nodes.py
repo_url = shared.get("repo_url")
local_dir = shared.get("local_dir")
project_name = shared.get("project_name")

if not project_name:
    if repo_url:
        project_name = repo_url.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1].removesuffix(".git")
    else:
        project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(local_dir))
    shared["project_name"] = project_name
The method resolves whether the source is local or remote and sets the shared project_name. It extracts path-filtering rules directly from shared["include_patterns"] and shared["exclude_patterns"], ensuring that downstream crawling operations adhere to configured file-size ceilings.

docs.title: FetchRepo.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: dict) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:

Description: Dispatches file harvesting to either crawl_github_files or crawl_local_files depending on whether repo_url is defined. Converts the returned file map into an indexed list of (path, content) tuples and validates that at least one file was captured.

Parameters: * prep_res (dict): Ingestion configuration packet returned by prep().

Returns: * list[tuple[str, str]]: An ordered collection of 2-tuples containing relative file paths and decoded UTF-8 string contents.

Raises: * ValueError: Raised if the crawler finds zero matching files, indicating invalid directory paths or overly restrictive inclusion/exclusion glob patterns.

Example: 

# Extracted from FetchRepo.exec() implementation in nodes.py
if prep_res["repo_url"]:
    emit("CRAWL_REPOSITORY", url=prep_res["repo_url"])
    result = crawl_github_files(
        repo_url=prep_res["repo_url"],
        token=prep_res["token"],
        include_patterns=prep_res["include_patterns"],
        exclude_patterns=prep_res["exclude_patterns"],
        max_file_size=prep_res["max_file_size"],
        use_relative_paths=prep_res["use_relative_paths"],
    )
else:
    emit("CRAWL_DIRECTORY", path=prep_res["local_dir"])
    result = crawl_local_files(
        directory=prep_res["local_dir"],
        include_patterns=prep_res["include_patterns"],
        exclude_patterns=prep_res["exclude_patterns"],
        max_file_size=prep_res["max_file_size"],
        use_relative_paths=prep_res["use_relative_paths"],
    )

files_list = list(result.get("files", {}).items())
if len(files_list) == 0:
    raise ValueError("No matching files found. Check your directory and include/exclude patterns.")
This execution routine emits real-time telemetry via output.emit to notify observers whether a local directory or remote Git URL is being scanned. The resulting file content dictionary is projected into a list of tuples to guarantee deterministic indexing across all downstream LLM context builders.

def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):

docs.title: ContextRouter.prep()
docs.text: Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

docs.title: Phase 1: Directory Tree Generation & API Reference Mode Short-Circuit
docs.text:
files_data = shared["files"]
max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)

shared["max_tokens"] = max_tokens
directory_tree = build_directory_tree(files_data)

if shared.get("mode", "tutorial") == "api-reference":
    # One chapter per file, packed by WriteChapters itself: no routing budget is needed.
    emit("CAPACITY_API_REF_MODE")
    return ("deterministic", files_data, 0, shared.get("batch_size", 50), None, None, directory_tree)
The node resolves the active model context ceiling using resolve_max_tokens and generates a structural directory tree of the repository. When operating under api-reference mode, token routing calculations are bypassed entirely, immediately selecting the "deterministic" route where chapters correspond directly to source files.

docs.title: Phase 2: Worst-Case Prompt Overhead Estimation
docs.text:
prompt_dir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "prompts")
max_template_tokens = 0
for subdir in ["tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", "sdk"]:
    for template_name in ["map_abstractions.md", "identify_abstractions.md", "draft_chapters.md"]:
        template_path = os.path.join(prompt_dir, subdir, template_name)
        if os.path.exists(template_path):
            with open(template_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                t = count_tokens(f.read())
            max_template_tokens = max(max_template_tokens, t)

tree_tokens = count_tokens(directory_tree)
chapter_listing_estimate = "\n".join(f"{i + 1}. {os.path.basename(path)} (doc: {path}.md)" for i, (path, _) in enumerate(files_data))
listing_tokens = count_tokens(chapter_listing_estimate)

prompt_overhead = max_template_tokens + tree_tokens + listing_tokens
emit(
    "CAPACITY_PROMPT_OVERHEAD",
    total=f"{prompt_overhead:,}",
    template=f"{max_template_tokens:,}",
    tree=f"{tree_tokens:,}",
    listing=f"{listing_tokens:,}",
)
To calculate available context space without overflowing model limits, the prep routine evaluates worst-case prompt framing overhead. It scans all prompt templates across all modes, measures the token volume of the rendered directory tree, and estimates the serialized chapter listing size.

docs.title: Phase 3: File Content Tokenization & Capacity Routing Decision
docs.text:
file_token_map = count_tokens_many([f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n" for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data)])
total_tokens = sum(file_token_map)

safety_limit = min(
    input_token_budget(max_tokens, resolve_thinking_level(shared, "identify_abstractions")),
    input_token_budget(max_tokens, resolve_thinking_level(shared, "map_abstractions")),
)
effective_limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead
force_batch = shared.get("force_batch", False)

if total_tokens > effective_limit and force_batch:
    emit("CAPACITY_EXCEEDS_FORCE", tokens=f"{total_tokens:,}", limit=f"{effective_limit:,}", safety=f"{safety_limit:,}", overhead=f"{prompt_overhead:,}")
elif total_tokens > effective_limit:
    emit("CAPACITY_EXCEEDS", tokens=f"{total_tokens:,}", limit=f"{effective_limit:,}", safety=f"{safety_limit:,}", overhead=f"{prompt_overhead:,}")
elif force_batch:
    emit("CAPACITY_FITS_FORCE", tokens=f"{total_tokens:,}", limit=f"{effective_limit:,}", safety=f"{safety_limit:,}", overhead=f"{prompt_overhead:,}")
else:
    emit("CAPACITY_FITS", tokens=f"{total_tokens:,}", limit=f"{effective_limit:,}", safety=f"{safety_limit:,}", overhead=f"{prompt_overhead:,}")
    return ("direct", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50), None, None, directory_tree)

return ("batch", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50), file_token_map, count_tokens, directory_tree)
The node tokenizes every file entry in parallel via count_tokens_many. It subtracts prompt overhead from the reasoning-adjusted input budget to establish an effective_limit. If the total codebase tokens fit within this limit (and force_batch is False), the node routes to "direct"; otherwise, it routes to "batch".

docs.title: ContextRouter.exec()
docs.text: Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> str | list[list[tuple[int, str, str]]]:

docs.title: Phase 1: Direct and Deterministic Pass-Through
docs.text:
route, files_data, effective_limit, batch_size, file_token_map, _count_tokens, _directory_tree = prep_res
emit_raw(
    "DEBUG",
    f"NODE EXEC | node=ContextRouter | action=route_decision | route={route} | files={len(files_data)} | effective_limit={effective_limit:,}",
    dest="LOG",
)

if route == "direct":
    return "direct"
if route == "deterministic":
    return "deterministic"
For the "direct" and "deterministic" routes, no batch partitioning is required. The execution method simply passes through the route string to indicate the next DAG transition.

dir_groups = defaultdict(list)
for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
    dir_groups[os.path.dirname(path)].append((i, path, content, file_token_map[i]))

batches = []
for dirname in sorted(dir_groups.keys()):
    current_batch = []
    current_tokens = 0

    for i, path, content, tokens in dir_groups[dirname]:
        if current_batch and (current_tokens + tokens > effective_limit or len(current_batch) >= batch_size):
            batches.append(current_batch)
            current_batch = []
            current_tokens = 0

        current_batch.append((i, path, content))
        current_tokens += tokens

    if current_batch:
        batches.append(current_batch)
For "batch" routing, files are grouped by their parent directory to preserve structural coherence. Files within each directory are packed into batches, ensuring neither effective_limit nor batch_size (default 50) is exceeded. Directory boundaries are strictly maintained—files from different directories are never mixed into the same batch.

Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: tuple, exec_res: list[int]) -> str:

Description: Constructs one-to-one module abstractions for every retained code file. Sorts the chapter order by directory depth (deepest leaf files first) and alphabetical path, ensuring utility dependencies are documented before orchestrators.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global workflow state dictionary. * prep_res (tuple): Input tuple from prep(). * exec_res (list[int]): Filtered list of integer file indices from exec().

# Extracted from DeterministicFileMapper.post() implementation in nodes.py
for idx, (file_path, _content) in enumerate(files):
    if idx not in valid_indices:
        emit("SKIP_NON_CODE_FILE", path=file_path)
        continue

    clean_name = os.path.basename(file_path)
    modules.append(
        {"name": clean_name, "description": f"Internal API reference for `{file_path}`", "files": [idx], "original_path": file_path}
    )
    chapter_order.append(len(modules) - 1)

shared["abstractions"] = modules

    chapter_order,
    key=lambda idx: (
        -modules[idx]["original_path"].count("/") - modules[idx]["original_path"].count(os.sep),
        modules[idx]["original_path"].lower(),
    ),
)

Depth-first sorting ensures that utility modules (e.g., utils/token_utils.py) are processed before top-level entry points (e.g., main.py). This allows subsequent chapters to reference previously generated technical summaries.

docs.title: Phase 2: LLM Dispatch & YAML Index Validation
docs.text:
response = call_llm(
    prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level, step="identify_abstractions"
)
abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)
if not isinstance(abstractions, list):
    raise ValueError("LLM Output is not a list")

validated_abstractions = []
for item in abstractions:
    if not isinstance(item, dict) or not all(k in item for k in ["name", "description", "file_indices"]):
        raise ValueError(f"Missing keys in abstraction item: {item}")

    validated_indices = []
    for idx_entry in item["file_indices"]:
        idx_str = str(idx_entry).split("#")[0].strip()
        if "-" in idx_str:
            parts = idx_str.split("-")
            if len(parts) == 2:
                start_idx = parse_file_index(parts[0])
                end_idx = parse_file_index(parts[1])
                if start_idx is not None and end_idx is not None:
                    validated_indices.extend(idx for idx in range(start_idx, end_idx + 1) if 0 <= idx < total_files_count)
                continue
        idx = parse_file_index(idx_str)
        if idx is not None and 0 <= idx < total_files_count:
            validated_indices.append(idx)

    item["files"] = sorted(set(validated_indices))
    validated_abstractions.append({"name": item["name"], "description": item["description"], "files": item["files"]})
The model response is deserialized via parse_yaml_response. The validation logic handles index formats produced by LLMs, including annotated strings ("3 # path"), raw integers, and integer ranges ("2-5"), clamping indices to valid repository bounds [0, total_files_count).

docs.title: AnalyzeRelationships.prep()
docs.text: Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

docs.title: Phase 1: Context Preparation & Token Budget Computation
docs.text:
abstractions = shared["abstractions"]
files_data = shared["files"]
project_name = shared["project_name"]
language = shared.get("language", "english")
use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)
thinking_level = resolve_thinking_level(shared, "analyze_relationships")
num_abstractions = len(abstractions)

context = "Identified Abstractions:\n"
all_relevant_indices = set()
abstraction_info_for_prompt = []
for i, abstr in enumerate(abstractions):
    file_indices_str = ", ".join(map(str, abstr["files"]))
    info_line = f"- Index {i}: {abstr['name']} (Relevant file indices: [{file_indices_str}])\n  Description: {abstr['description']}"
    context += info_line + "\n"
    abstraction_info_for_prompt.append(f"{i} # {abstr['name']}")
    all_relevant_indices.update(abstr["files"])

context += "\nRelevant File Snippets (per abstraction, budget-aware):\n"
max_tokens = shared.get("max_tokens", 100000)
safety_limit = input_token_budget(max_tokens, thinking_level)
prompt_overhead = 2000
current_tokens = count_tokens(context)
total_budget = safety_limit - current_tokens - prompt_overhead
The node formats baseline descriptions for all identified abstractions and measures their token footprint. It calculates the remaining prompt capacity available for source file snippets by subtracting prompt overhead and existing context from the input token safety limit.

docs.title: Phase 2: Two-Pass Equal Share and Rollover Budget Redistribution
docs.text:
abstr_file_data = []
for abstr in abstractions:
    sized = []
    for idx in abstr["files"]:
        if 0 <= idx < len(files_data):
            path, file_content = files_data[idx]
            entry = f"\n--- File: {idx} # {path} ---\n{file_content}\n"
            sized.append((idx, path, file_content, count_tokens(entry)))
    sized.sort(key=lambda x: x[3], reverse=True)
    abstr_file_data.append(sized)

per_abstr_budget = total_budget // max(num_abstractions, 1)
included_indices = set()
abstr_results = []

for _i, sized in enumerate(abstr_file_data):
    budget = per_abstr_budget
    included_files, remaining_files = [], []
    for idx, path, file_content, tokens in sized:
        if idx in included_indices:
            included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
            continue
        if tokens <= budget:
            included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
            budget -= tokens
            included_indices.add(idx)
        else:
            remaining_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
    abstr_results.append((included_files, remaining_files, budget))

total_unused = sum(r[2] for r in abstr_results)
if total_unused > 0:
    for i, (included_files, remaining_files, _unused) in enumerate(abstr_results):
        if not remaining_files or total_unused <= 0:
            continue
        still_remaining = []
        for idx, path, file_content, tokens in remaining_files:
            if idx in included_indices:
                included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                continue
            if tokens <= total_unused:
                included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                total_unused -= tokens
                included_indices.add(idx)
            else:
                still_remaining.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
        abstr_results[i] = (included_files, still_remaining, 0)
To prevent early abstractions from consuming all context budget, the algorithm enforces a two-pass allocation. Pass 1 divides the available budget equally among all abstractions, packing their largest, most architecturally significant files first. Pass 2 aggregates unused surplus budgets across smaller abstractions and redistributes it to abstractions with pending files.

docs.title: Phase 3: Final File Snippet Context Assembly
docs.text:
for i, abstr in enumerate(abstractions):
    included_files, remaining_files, _ = abstr_results[i]
    if included_files or remaining_files:
        context += f"\n--- Abstraction {i}: {abstr['name']} ---\n"
        for idx, path, file_content, _tokens in included_files:
            if file_content is not None:
                context += f"\n--- File: {idx} # {path} ---\n{file_content}\n"
            else:
                context += f"  (File {idx} # {path} -- already shown above)\n"
        if remaining_files:
            rest_list = ", ".join(f"{idx} # {p}" for idx, p, _c, _t in remaining_files)
            context += f"  Other files (path only, budget exhausted): {rest_list}\n"

return (
    context, "\n".join(abstraction_info_for_prompt), num_abstractions,
    project_name, language, use_cache, thinking_level,
    shared.get("advanced_mode", False), shared.get("max_tokens", 100000),
    shared.get("mode", "tutorial"),
)
The final context string is assembled by appending file contents included in the budget. Files already emitted in earlier abstractions are marked as previously displayed to avoid duplicate tokens. Files omitted due to budget exhaustion are appended as path-only references.

docs.title: Phase 2: Response Deserialization & Relationship Index Normalization
docs.text:
relationships_data = parse_yaml_response(response)
if not isinstance(relationships_data, dict) or not all(k in relationships_data for k in ["summary", "relationships"]):
    raise ValueError("LLM output is not a dict or missing keys ('summary', 'relationships')")

validated_relationships = []
for rel in relationships_data["relationships"]:
    if not isinstance(rel, dict) or not all(k in rel for k in ["from_abstraction", "to_abstraction", "label"]):
        raise ValueError(f"Missing keys (expected from_abstraction, to_abstraction, label) in relationship item: {rel}")

    from_nums = re.findall(r"\d+", str(rel["from_abstraction"]).split("#")[0].strip())
    to_nums = re.findall(r"\d+", str(rel["to_abstraction"]).split("#")[0].strip())
    if not from_nums or not to_nums:
        raise ValueError("Missing valid integer for from_abstraction or to_abstraction.")

    from_idx, to_idx = int(from_nums[0]), int(to_nums[0])
    if not (0 <= from_idx < num_abstractions and 0 <= to_idx < num_abstractions):
        emit("WARN_INVALID_RELATIONSHIP", from_idx=from_idx, to_idx=to_idx, max_idx=num_abstractions - 1)
        continue
    validated_relationships.append({"from": from_idx, "to": to_idx, "label": rel["label"]})

return {"summary": relationships_data["summary"], "details": validated_relationships}
Deserializes the YAML response and strictly validates relationship keys. It extracts integer abstraction indices using regular expressions, discarding invalid or out-of-range edges while preserving directional dependencies (from $\rightarrow$ to) and descriptive connection labels.

docs.title: OrderChapters.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public (decorated with @safe_exec) Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> list[int]:

Description: Calls the LLM to establish narrative chapter order and validates the returned sequence to ensure completeness, no duplicate indices, and strict bijection with existing abstractions.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Prepared ordering context from prep().

Returns: * list[int]: An ordered permutation of integer abstraction indices.

Raises: * ValueError: Raised if the output is not a list, contains invalid indices, contains duplicates, or omits abstractions.

Example: 

# Extracted from OrderChapters.exec() implementation in nodes.py
ordered_indices_raw = parse_yaml_response(response)
if not isinstance(ordered_indices_raw, list):
    raise ValueError("LLM output is not a list")

ordered_indices = []
seen_indices = set()
for entry in ordered_indices_raw:
    idx = int(entry.split("#")[0].strip()) if isinstance(entry, str) and "#" in entry else int(str(entry).strip())
    if not (0 <= idx < num_abstractions):
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid index {idx} in ordered list. Max index is {num_abstractions - 1}.")
    if idx in seen_indices:
        raise ValueError(f"Duplicate index {idx} found in ordered list.")
    ordered_indices.append(idx)
    seen_indices.add(idx)

if len(ordered_indices) != num_abstractions:
    raise ValueError(f"Ordered list length ({len(ordered_indices)}) does not match abstractions count.")
return ordered_indices
Defensive parsing ensures the LLM's ordered list forms a valid permutation of the abstraction indices. Any missing abstraction or duplicated index triggers an immediate ValueError, causing PocketFlow to retry the generation.

docs.title: WriteChapters.exec()
docs.text: Visibility: Public (decorated with @safe_exec) Signature: def exec(self, item: dict) -> dict:

docs.title: Phase 1: File Context Preparation & Incremental Manifest Cache Check
docs.text:
abstraction_name = item["abstraction_details"]["name"]
chapter_num = item["chapter_num"]
project_name = item.get("project_name")
language = item.get("language", "english")
use_cache = item.get("use_cache", True)
thinking_level = item.get("thinking_level", None)
summary_thinking_level = item.get("summary_thinking_level", thinking_level)
mode = item.get("mode", "tutorial")
is_mkdocs = item.get("mkdocs", False)
incremental = item.get("incremental", False)
output_dir = item.get("output_dir", "output")
filename = item.get("filename")
max_tokens = item.get("max_tokens", 100000)

file_context_str = "\n\n".join(
    f"--- File: {idx_path.split('# ')[1] if '# ' in idx_path else idx_path} ---\n{content}"
    for idx_path, content in item["related_files_content_map"].items()
)

current_hash = None
if incremental and output_dir:
    hasher = hashlib.md5()
    hasher.update(item.get("generation_signature", "").encode("utf-8"))
    hasher.update(file_context_str.encode("utf-8"))
    current_hash = hasher.hexdigest()

    manifest_path = os.path.join(output_dir, project_name, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
    if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
        try:
            with open(manifest_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                manifest = json.load(f)
            cached_entry = manifest.get(abstraction_name)
            cached_hash = cached_entry.get("hash") if isinstance(cached_entry, dict) else (cached_entry if isinstance(cached_entry, str) else None)
            cached_summary = cached_entry.get("summary") if isinstance(cached_entry, dict) else None

            if cached_hash == current_hash:
                file_path = os.path.join(output_dir, project_name, "docs", "api", filename) if is_mkdocs else os.path.join(output_dir, project_name, filename)
                if os.path.exists(file_path):
                    emit("CACHE_HIT_SKIP", name=abstraction_name)
                    with open(file_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                        cached_content = f.read()
                    clean_content = cached_content
                    if is_mkdocs and clean_content.startswith("---"):
                        parts = clean_content.split("---", 2)
                        if len(parts) >= 3:
                            clean_content = parts[2].strip()
                    self.chapters_written_so_far.append(clean_content)
                    if cached_summary:
                        self.chapter_summaries.append(cached_summary)
                    return {"content": clean_content, "hash": current_hash, "name": abstraction_name, "summary": self.chapter_summaries[-1]}
        except Exception as e:
            emit("WARN_MANIFEST_CACHE_FAIL", error=e)
When running in --incremental mode, the node computes an MD5 checksum over the generation signature and the file context string. If .doc_cache_manifest.json contains a matching hash and the chapter file exists on disk, generation is skipped and cached contents and summaries are loaded into instance state directly.

docs.title: Phase 2: Chronological Summary Windowing & 50% Context Pruning
docs.text:
prev_chapters_budget = int(max_tokens * 0.50)
prev_chapters_tokens = 0
if self.chapter_summaries:
    selected_summaries = []
    running_tokens = 0
    for summary in reversed(self.chapter_summaries):
        summary_tokens = count_tokens(summary)
        if running_tokens + summary_tokens > prev_chapters_budget and selected_summaries:
            break
        selected_summaries.append(summary)
        running_tokens += summary_tokens

    selected_summaries.reverse()
    separator_tokens = count_tokens("\n---\n")
    prev_chapters_tokens = running_tokens + separator_tokens * (len(selected_summaries) - 1)

    if len(selected_summaries) < len(self.chapter_summaries):
        dropped = len(self.chapter_summaries) - len(selected_summaries)
        emit("PREV_CHAPTERS_TRIMMED", dropped=dropped, total=len(self.chapter_summaries), budget=f"{prev_chapters_budget:,}", kept=len(selected_summaries))
        window_note = f"[{dropped} earlier chapter summaries omitted — showing {len(selected_summaries)} most recent for context budget]"
        previous_chapters_summary = window_note + "\n---\n" + "\n---\n".join(selected_summaries)
    else:
        previous_chapters_summary = "\n---\n".join(self.chapter_summaries)
else:
    previous_chapters_summary = ""
To avoid the $O(n^2)$ token accumulation caused by injecting full previous chapters into prompts, the node uses concise LLM summaries (3–5 sentences per chapter). These summaries are capped at 50% of the active context window, traversing from newest to oldest to prune older context when limits are reached.

docs.title: WriteChapters.exec_fallback()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec_fallback(self, item: dict, exc: Exception) -> dict:

Description: Fallback handler invoked by PocketFlow when a chapter fails across all retry attempts. Emits a localized warning, appends a placeholder summary to keep instance lists aligned, and returns a fallback page with hash: None so it will be regenerated on the next run.

Parameters: * item (dict): The batch work item that encountered terminal failures. * exc (Exception): The unhandled exception triggering the fallback.

Returns: * dict: Dictionary containing placeholder content, null hash, abstraction name, and unavailable notice summary.

Example: 

# Extracted from WriteChapters.exec_fallback() implementation in nodes.py
name = item["abstraction_details"]["name"]
chapter_num = item["chapter_num"]
emit("WARN_CHAPTER_FALLBACK", chapter_num=chapter_num, name=name.strip(), error=exc)
notice = get("UI_CHAPTER_UNAVAILABLE")
summary = f"{get('UI_CHAPTER')} {chapter_num} — {name.strip()}:\n{notice}"
self.chapter_summaries.append(summary)
return {"content": f"# {name.strip()}\n\n{notice}\n", "hash": None, "name": name, "summary": summary}
This fallback ensures that a failure in a single chapter does not abort a multi-hour documentation run across dozens of files.

docs.title: WriteChapters.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: list[dict], exec_res_list: list[dict]) -> None:

Description: Gathers all drafted chapter contents into shared["chapters"], writes updated .doc_cache_manifest.json records to disk when --incremental is active, persists chapter summaries to shared["chapter_summaries"], and frees batch instance memory.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global workflow state dictionary. * prep_res (list[dict]): Initial batch preparation records. * exec_res_list (list[dict]): List of results returned across all chapter executions.

Returns: * None

Example: 

# Extracted from WriteChapters.post() implementation in nodes.py
shared["chapters"] = [res["content"] for res in exec_res_list]

if shared.get("incremental"):
    output_dir = os.path.join(shared.get("output_dir", "output"), shared.get("project_name"))
    os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
    manifest_path = os.path.join(output_dir, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")

    manifest = {}
    if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
        try:
            with open(manifest_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                manifest = json.load(f)
        except Exception:
            pass

    for res in exec_res_list:
        if res.get("hash") and res.get("name"):
            manifest[res["name"]] = {"hash": res["hash"], "summary": res.get("summary", "")}
        elif res.get("name"):
            manifest.pop(res["name"], None)

    with open(manifest_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)

shared["chapter_summaries"] = list(self.chapter_summaries)
del self.chapters_written_so_far
del self.chapter_summaries
emit("DONE_ALL_CHAPTERS", count=len(exec_res_list))
emit_step_subtotals("write_chapters", "chapter_summary")
The method cleans up temporary instance collections (del self.chapters_written_so_far) to prevent memory leaks across long-lived graph processes. It also updates the on-disk manifest, removing entries for truncated or placeholder chapters so they are recomputed on subsequent runs.

docs.text:
project_name = shared["project_name"]
output_base_dir = shared.get("output_dir", "output")

    node_id = f"A{i}"
    sanitized_name = abstr["name"].replace('"', "").replace("\n", " ").strip()
    mermaid_lines.append(f'    {node_id}("{sanitized_name}")')
for rel in relationships_data["details"]:
    from_node_id = f"A{rel['from']}"
    to_node_id = f"A{rel['to']}"
    edge_label = rel["label"].replace('"', "").replace("\n", " ")
    if len(edge_label) > 30:
        edge_label = edge_label[:27] + "..."
    mermaid_lines.append(f'    {from_node_id} -- "{edge_label}" --> {to_node_id}')

incoming = {f"A{i}": 0 for i in range(len(abstractions))}
for rel in relationships_data["details"]:
    incoming[f"A{rel['to']}"] += 1
entry_nodes = [nid for nid, inc in incoming.items() if inc >= 2]
if entry_nodes:
    mermaid_lines.append("    classDef entryNode stroke:#d33,stroke-width:3px,fill:#fff5f5")
    mermaid_lines.extend(f"    class {node_id} entryNode" for node_id in entry_nodes)

mermaid_diagram = "\n".join(mermaid_lines)
