docs.title: _get_client()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _get_client() -> anthropic.Anthropic:

Description: Lazily initializes and returns the singleton anthropic.Anthropic client instance stored in the module-level _client variable. The client is instantiated with max_retries=3, which handles standard 408, 409, 429, and 5xx transient server backoffs internally before escalating back to pipeline-level retry mechanisms.

Parameters: None.

Returns: * anthropic.Anthropic: The configured singleton client instance.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _get_client():
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        # SDK resolves credentials (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / AUTH_TOKEN / ant profile) and
        # ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL itself. SDK retries 408/409/429/5xx with backoff;
        # PocketFlow node retries sit on top of this.
        _client = anthropic.Anthropic(max_retries=3)
    return _client
The internal client instance is managed as a module-scoped singleton because inference runs in this architecture are single-threaded and sequential. The Anthropic SDK automatically inspects system environment variables such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL upon instantiation.

docs.title: _matches()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _matches(model: str, prefixes: tuple[str, ...] | list[str]) -> bool:

Description: Utility helper that checks if a model name starts with any prefix in a given collection.

Parameters: * model (str): The model identifier string. * prefixes (tuple[str, ...] | list[str]): A sequence of model prefix strings.

Returns: * bool: True if any prefix matches the start of model, False otherwise.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _matches(model: str, prefixes) -> bool:
    return any(model.startswith(p) for p in prefixes)
This helper centralizes prefix-based matching throughout the module. It is called by uses_adaptive_thinking() to identify adaptive models and by _fallback_config() to detect models subject to safety classifier fallbacks.

docs.title: _fallback_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _fallback_config(model: str) -> tuple[list[str], dict]:

Description: Determines the required server-side fallback beta headers and body configurations based on the ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS environment variable and model compatibility. If the setting is disabled, set to "off", or previously flagged as unsupported via runtime 400 errors (_fallbacks_disabled), it returns empty structures.

Parameters: * model (str): Target model identifier string.

Returns: * tuple[list[str], dict]: A 2-tuple of (betas, extra_body). When fallbacks are enabled, betas contains beta feature flags (e.g., ["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"]) and extra_body contains fallback model routing rules.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _fallback_config(model: str) -> tuple[list[str], dict]:
    """Return (betas, extra_body) for server-side refusal fallbacks, or empty when disabled."""
    setting = (os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS") or "default").strip()
    if _fallbacks_disabled or setting.lower() == "off":
        return [], {}
    if setting.lower() == "default":
        if not _matches(model, _FALLBACK_PREFIXES):
            return [], {}
        return [_FALLBACK_DEFAULT_BETA], {"fallbacks": "default"}
    targets = [m.strip() for m in setting.split(",") if m.strip()]
    return [_FALLBACK_LIST_BETA], {"fallbacks": [{"model": m} for m in targets]}
Server-side fallbacks allow requests rejected by safety classifiers on frontier models (e.g., Opus 5.x, Fable 5.x) to route automatically to secondary fallback models. If a comma-delimited list of models is passed via ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS, the helper constructs a custom target list using the fallback list beta header server-side-fallback-2026-06-01.

docs.title: _build_request()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _build_request(prompt: str, model: str, effort: str | None, max_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:

Description: Constructs the complete payload dictionary and beta header list required by the Anthropic Messages API. It configures adaptive reasoning dictionaries, legacy budget token bounds, ephemeral prompt caching options, and server-side fallback payloads.

Parameters: * prompt (str): User prompt content string. * model (str): Target model name. * effort (str | None): Effort level name or None. * max_tokens (int): Maximum generation limit.

Returns: * tuple[dict, list[str]]: A 2-tuple consisting of the parameter dictionary (params) and a list of beta feature strings (betas).

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _build_request(prompt: str, model: str, effort: str | None, max_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:
    params = {
        "model": model,
        "max_tokens": max_tokens,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    }
    if uses_adaptive_thinking(model):
        if effort or _matches(model, _THINKING_BY_DEFAULT_PREFIXES):
            thinking = {"type": "adaptive"}
            if is_debug():
                # Readable reasoning summaries go to the log file (never to stdout).
                thinking["display"] = "summarized"
            params["thinking"] = thinking
        if effort:
            params["output_config"] = {"effort": effort}
    elif effort:
        budget = min(_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL[effort], max_tokens - 1_024)
        if budget >= 1_024:
            params["thinking"] = {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": budget}

    if (os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHE") or "off").strip().lower() == "on":
        params["cache_control"] = {"type": "ephemeral"}

    betas, extra_body = _fallback_config(model)
    if extra_body:
        params["extra_body"] = extra_body
    return params, betas
This helper adapts payloads based on model family traits. When targeting adaptive thinking architectures, it builds an {"type": "adaptive"} structure and optionally sets display: "summarized" when debug logging is active. For legacy reasoning models, it sets fixed token budgets derived from _BUDGET_BY_LEVEL, ensuring at least 1,024 tokens remain allocated for output synthesis.

docs.title: _resolve_max_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _resolve_max_tokens(prompt_tokens: int, model: str, effort: str | None) -> tuple[int, int]:

Description: Computes the optimal generation budget (wanted) and the maximum permissible ceiling (ceiling). It takes into account the model's native context window, the model's output cap, external environment caps (ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS), and a safety margin defined by ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN.

Parameters: * prompt_tokens (int): Scaled token estimation of the prompt text. * model (str): Model identifier string. * effort (str | None): Desired reasoning effort.

Returns: * tuple[int, int]: A 2-tuple containing (wanted, ceiling), where wanted is the requested budget clamped to the available ceiling, and ceiling is the absolute upper boundary allowed for retries.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _resolve_max_tokens(prompt_tokens: int, model: str, effort: str | None) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Return (max_tokens, ceiling): the planned budget and the largest budget allowed."""
    context_window, output_cap = get_model_limits(model)
    cap = anthropic_output_cap()
    wanted = anthropic_planned_output(model, effort)  # same value input_token_budget reserved

    room = max(context_window - prompt_tokens - ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN, 4_096)
    ceiling = min(output_cap, room, cap) if cap else min(output_cap, room)
    if ceiling < wanted:
        # Small shortfalls (template overhead on a budget-packed prompt) are expected; only report real cuts.
        if ceiling < wanted * 0.9:
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED", wanted=f"{wanted:,}", available=f"{ceiling:,}")
        wanted = ceiling
    return wanted, ceiling
The available context headroom (room) subtracts prompt tokens and safety margins (ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN) from the total context window. If the calculated ceiling reduces the planned output tokens by more than 10%, WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED is emitted to alert the operator of token budget restrictions.

docs.title: _stream_message()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _stream_message(params: dict, betas: list[str]):

Description: Dispatches a streamed Messages API call through the Anthropic SDK client, returning the aggregated Message object upon stream completion.

Parameters: * params (dict): The payload dictionary. * betas (list[str]): List of beta feature headers.

Returns: * anthropic.types.Message: The fully accumulated message object.

Raises: * anthropic.APIError: If the API call fails during streaming.

Example: 

def _stream_message(params: dict, betas: list[str]):
    client = _get_client()
    if betas:
        with client.beta.messages.stream(betas=betas, **params) as stream:
            return stream.get_final_message()
    with client.messages.stream(**params) as stream:
        return stream.get_final_message()
The helper selects either client.beta.messages.stream or client.messages.stream based on whether experimental beta feature headers are present. Context managers guarantee that the stream is cleanly consumed and connection resources are released once stream.get_final_message() resolves.

docs.title: _fallback_rejected()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _fallback_rejected(error_text: str, params: dict) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether an HTTP 400 Bad Request error indicates an unsupported server-side fallback configuration (such as invalid beta headers or lack of account entitlement) rather than a malformed user payload.

Parameters: * error_text (str): The error string from anthropic.BadRequestError. * params (dict): The request parameter dictionary.

Returns: * bool: True if the error was caused by server-side fallback rejection, False otherwise.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _fallback_rejected(error_text: str, params: dict) -> bool:
    """True when a 400 rejects the fallback feature itself (beta header not enabled, or
    `fallbacks: "default"` unsupported for this model/account) — not a user config error."""
    text = error_text.lower()
    if "anthropic-beta" in text and "server-side-fallback" in text:
        return True
    return params.get("extra_body", {}).get("fallbacks") == "default" and "fallbacks" in text
This inspection utility prevents persistent pipeline failures when experimental fallback betas are not provisioned on an API key. By distinguishing syntax errors from permission rejections, it enables graceful runtime downgrades.

docs.title: _send()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _send(params: dict, betas: list[str]):

Description: Wraps _stream_message in defensive error handling to gracefully degrade requests if server-side fallbacks are rejected. When a fallback-related 400 error occurs, it permanently disables fallbacks for the remainder of the runtime session (_fallbacks_disabled = True), strips extra_body from the request parameters, and resends the request without beta headers.

Parameters: * params (dict): Request parameters. * betas (list[str]): Beta feature header flags.

Returns: * anthropic.types.Message: The received final message.

Raises: * anthropic.BadRequestError: Re-raised if the 400 error is unrelated to fallback mechanics. * anthropic.APIError: Any other upstream API communication failures.

Example: 

def _send(params: dict, betas: list[str]):
    """Send one streamed request; disable fallbacks for the run if the feature is unavailable."""
    global _fallbacks_disabled
    try:
        return _stream_message(params, betas)
    except anthropic.BadRequestError as e:
        if "extra_body" in params and _fallback_rejected(str(e), params):
            _fallbacks_disabled = True
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED", error=str(e))
            retry_params = {k: v for k, v in params.items() if k != "extra_body"}
            return _stream_message(retry_params, [])
        raise
This error recovery path allows the application to remain functional across varying API tier subscriptions. If an account lacks access to the server-side fallback beta, the system logs WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED and immediately retries the base request without interruption.

docs.title: _price()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _price(model: str, tokens_in: int, tokens_out: int, cache_read: int, cache_write: int) -> float | None:

Description: Computes the estimated USD cost of an execution using the internal _PRICING lookup table. Matches model names using longest-prefix comparison against known models, factoring in base inputs, outputs, cache reads, and ephemeral cache writes (billed at 1.25x the standard input rate).

Parameters: * model (str): Served model string. * tokens_in (int): Uncached input tokens. * tokens_out (int): Total generated output tokens. * cache_read (int): Prompt tokens read from cache. * cache_write (int): Prompt tokens written to 5-minute ephemeral cache.

Returns: * float | None: Estimated dollar cost rounded to precision, or None if the model has no entry in _PRICING.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _price(model: str, tokens_in: int, tokens_out: int, cache_read: int, cache_write: int) -> float | None:
    price = next((_PRICING[k] for k in sorted(_PRICING, key=len, reverse=True) if (model or "").startswith(k)), None)
    if price is None:
        return None
    p_in, p_out, p_read = price
    return (tokens_in * p_in + tokens_out * p_out + cache_read * p_read + cache_write * p_in * 1.25) / 1_000_000
Prefix sorting ensures that more specific model designations (e.g., claude-opus-5-5) match before broader base prefixes (claude-opus-5). The token counts are normalized per million tokens as specified by provider billing standards.

docs.title: _tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _tokens(usage) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:

Description: Extracts standard input, output, cache-read, and cache-creation token quantities from an Anthropic SDK Usage object, substituting 0 for absent or null fields.

Parameters: * usage: An Anthropic SDK usage object or iteration entry.

Returns: * tuple[int, int, int, int]: (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens).

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _tokens(usage) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    return (
        getattr(usage, "input_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "output_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "cache_read_input_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "cache_creation_input_tokens", 0) or 0,
    )
This utility provides safe attribute retrieval against the response's usage schema across various SDK minor versions, preventing AttributeError exceptions when cache metric properties are omitted.

docs.title: _thinking_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _thinking_tokens(usage) -> int:

Description: Safely extracts the number of reasoning tokens generated during chain-of-thought processing from the nested output_tokens_details structure of a usage record.

Parameters: * usage: SDK usage object.

Returns: * int: Count of generated thinking tokens, or 0 if absent.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _thinking_tokens(usage) -> int:
    details = getattr(usage, "output_tokens_details", None)
    return getattr(details, "thinking_tokens", 0) or 0
Claude models with adaptive or budgeted reasoning report their thinking token volume inside output_tokens_details. This helper isolates the value for independent reporting in telemetry feeds and debug logs.

docs.title: _declined_before_output()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _declined_before_output(message) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether a message was refused by safety mechanisms prior to generating any output tokens. Requests refused before producing output are not billed by the provider.

Parameters: * message: The Anthropic response message object.

Returns: * bool: True if stop_reason == "refusal" and output_tokens is zero, False otherwise.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _declined_before_output(message) -> bool:
    """A refusal with no output tokens at all is not billed (the same rule as for fallback iterations)."""
    return getattr(message, "stop_reason", None) == "refusal" and not (getattr(message.usage, "output_tokens", 0) or 0)
This check ensures that cost calculation routines align with Anthropic's billing guidelines. Requests halted by input-level safety evaluations incur zero cost.

docs.title: _billed_entries()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _billed_entries(message) -> list:

Description: Identifies and extracts all usage objects that should be recorded for billing. When server-side fallbacks occur, individual attempts are listed under message.usage.iterations. In this scenario, any iteration that generated output tokens is retained. If no iterations exist, the primary message.usage is returned, provided it was not refused before generating output.

Parameters: * message: The Anthropic Message response object.

Returns: * list: Collection of usage records subject to cost accounting.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _billed_entries(message) -> list:
    """Usage entries of the billed attempts: every usage.iterations entry with output (server-side
    fallbacks), else the top-level usage unless the request was declined before any output."""
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    if iterations:
        return [entry for entry in iterations if (getattr(entry, "output_tokens", 0) or 0) > 0]
    return [] if _declined_before_output(message) else [message.usage]
This entry-filtering logic handles multi-hop fallback invocations. By filtering out unbilled refusals across fallback attempts, it ensures billing metrics accurately reflect chargeable usage.

docs.title: _billed_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _billed_tokens(message) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int]:

Description: Aggregates token counts across all billable attempts returned by _billed_entries().

Parameters: * message: The Anthropic Message response object.

Returns: * tuple[int, int, int, int, int]: A 5-tuple of (total_in, out, cache_read, cache_write, thinking) where total_in encompasses uncached inputs, cache reads, and cache writes.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _billed_tokens(message) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int]:
    """(total input incl. cache read/write, output, cache_read, cache_write, thinking) summed over the
    billed attempts (_billed_entries), so token totals match _message_cost."""
    total_in = out = cache_read = cache_write = thinking = 0
    for entry in _billed_entries(message):
        tokens_in, tokens_out, read, write = _tokens(entry)
        total_in += tokens_in + read + write
        out += tokens_out
        cache_read += read
        cache_write += write
        thinking += _thinking_tokens(entry)
    return total_in, out, cache_read, cache_write, thinking
Summing across all billable attempts prevents discrepancies between token counts reported in logs and the monetary costs recorded in the ledger.

docs.title: _message_cost()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _message_cost(message, served_model: str) -> float | None:

Description: Computes the aggregate USD cost across all billable execution attempts within a response message. For fallback chains, each iteration is priced according to its specific model's pricing rates.

Parameters: * message: The Anthropic response message. * served_model (str): Fallback model identifier string if iteration-level model IDs are missing.

Returns: * float | None: Total USD cost, 0.0 for unbilled refusals, or None if pricing is unavailable for any involved model.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _message_cost(message, served_model: str) -> float | None:
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    if iterations:
        total, known = 0.0, True
        for entry in iterations:
            tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write = _tokens(entry)
            if tokens_out == 0:
                continue  # declined before any output (primary or fallback attempt): not billed
            cost = _price(getattr(entry, "model", None) or served_model, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write)
            known = known and cost is not None
            total += cost or 0.0
        return total if known else None
    if _declined_before_output(message):
        return 0.0  # declined before any output: not billed
    return _price(served_model, *_tokens(message.usage))
This calculation accurately accounts for requests that cycle through multiple models during fallback processing. For example, if an Opus request evaluates input tokens and transitions to a Sonnet fallback, the usage across each model is priced using its respective rate.

docs.title: _record_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _record_usage(message, raw_prompt_tokens: int, effort: str | None, elapsed: float, model: str = "", observe: bool = True) -> None:

Description: Records execution usage into the global accounting ledger via utils.llm_common.record_usage(), submits observed input token counts to utils.token_utils.observe_prompt_tokens() for dynamic ratio calibration, and outputs debug telemetry lines.

Parameters: * message: The Anthropic SDK Message object. * raw_prompt_tokens (int): Base tiktoken prompt token count. * effort (str | None): Active effort parameter string. * elapsed (float): Call duration in seconds. * model (str): Target requested model string. * observe (bool): When True, submits token ratios to dynamic calibration; when False (such as during truncation retries), calibration updates are skipped.

Returns: None.

Raises: None.

docs.title: Phase 1: Billed Entry Aggregation and Ledger Recording
docs.text:
from utils.token_utils import observe_prompt_tokens

    served_model = getattr(message, "model", "") or ""
    has_iterations = bool(getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None))
    entries = _billed_entries(message)
    if not entries:
        record_usage("ANTHROPIC", served_model, cost=0.0, measured=False)  # declined before any output: not billed
    # One ledger request per billed attempt (primary + fallback each billed at its own model's rate), so
    # request counts, per-request estimate deviation and the model list stay correct.
    for entry in entries:
        t_in, t_out, read, write = _tokens(entry)
        entry_model = (getattr(entry, "model", None) or served_model) if has_iterations else served_model
        record_usage(
            "ANTHROPIC",
            entry_model,
            input_tokens=t_in + read + write,
            output_tokens=t_out,
            thinking_tokens=_thinking_tokens(entry),
            cache_read=read,
            cache_write=write,
            cost=_price(entry_model, t_in, t_out, read, write) if has_iterations else _message_cost(message, served_model),
        )
Each billable attempt is recorded as a separate ledger entry under the ANTHROPIC provider key. This approach ensures multi-attempt fallbacks preserve accurate per-model request counts, ledger balance adjustments, and cache read/write breakdowns.

docs.title: Phase 2: Ratio Calibration and Diagnostic Logging
docs.text:
total_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write, thinking = _billed_tokens(message)  # totals for the debug line
    cost = _message_cost(message, served_model)

    # Observed Claude/tiktoken ratio of the attempt that produced this message (top-level usage),
    # fed to the calibration unless another model (server-side fallback) served it.
    tokens_in, _, read, write = _tokens(message.usage)
    attempt_in = tokens_in + read + write
    ratio = attempt_in / raw_prompt_tokens if raw_prompt_tokens else 0.0
    if observe and model and not _served_by_fallback(message):
        observe_prompt_tokens("ANTHROPIC", model, raw_prompt_tokens, attempt_in, served_model=served_model)
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"ANTHROPIC USAGE | model={served_model} | effort={effort or 'default'} | stop={message.stop_reason} | "
        f"in={total_in:,} | out={tokens_out:,} | thinking={thinking:,} | cache_read={cache_read:,} | cache_write={cache_write:,} | "
        f"est_cost={'$' + format(cost, '.4f') if cost is not None else 'n/a'} | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | observed_token_ratio={ratio:.2f}",
        dest="BOTH",
    )
This phase calculates the ratio of observed Anthropic input tokens to estimated tiktoken counts. If the call was fulfilled by the target model rather than a fallback, the ratio is submitted to observe_prompt_tokens() in token_utils.py to refine future budget estimations. Finally, a structured ANTHROPIC USAGE debug line is emitted to both stdout and log destinations.

docs.title: _log_thinking()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _log_thinking(message) -> None:

Description: Extracts summarized thinking content blocks from the message and logs them to the diagnostic log file when debug logging is active.

Parameters: * message: The Anthropic response message object.

Returns: None.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _log_thinking(message) -> None:
    for block in message.content:
        if getattr(block, "type", None) == "thinking" and getattr(block, "thinking", ""):
            emit_raw("DEBUG", f"THINKING SUMMARY:\n{block.thinking}", dest="LOG")
This utility iterates across the response's content blocks, extracting any entries where block.type == "thinking". It routes reasoning traces exclusively to the log destination (dest="LOG") to maintain clean, human-readable terminal output.

docs.title: _served_by_fallback()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _served_by_fallback(message) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether a response was completed by an automatic fallback model rather than the primary target model, by inspecting message content blocks and usage iteration types.

Parameters: * message: The Anthropic response message.

Returns: * bool: True if a fallback marker block or iteration is present, False otherwise.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _served_by_fallback(message) -> bool:
    if any(getattr(block, "type", None) == "fallback" for block in message.content):
        return True
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    return any(getattr(entry, "type", None) == "fallback_message" for entry in iterations)
This check is used by call_anthropic() and _record_usage() to update fallback metrics via count_event and bypass token calibration when output was generated by an alternate model.

docs.title: _extract_text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _extract_text(message) -> str:

Description: Concatenates all textual content blocks from an Anthropic message into a single response string, filtering out thinking blocks, tool requests, or metadata segments.

Parameters: * message: The Anthropic response message.

Returns: * str: Joined textual payload from all text blocks.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _extract_text(message) -> str:
    return "".join(block.text for block in message.content if getattr(block, "type", None) == "text")
This function separates reasoning artifacts and metadata blocks from the primary textual content, ensuring only the target answer is returned to downstream nodes.

docs.title: Pricing Directory (_PRICING)
docs.text:

docs.title: Refusal Trapping (LLMRefusalError)
docs.text:
When Claude's safety filters reject an incoming prompt, the response sets stop_reason == "refusal". call_anthropic() traps this stop reason, extracts the violation category from message.stop_details.category, records the event in telemetry using count_event("ANTHROPIC", "refusals"), emits WARN_ANTHROPIC_REFUSAL, and raises: 

raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="ANTHROPIC")
Upstream, call_llm.py intercepts LLMRefusalError to record the refusal signature in memory, preventing repeated execution attempts on rejected prompts.

docs.title: Truncation Detection and Single-Pass Retry
docs.text: Output truncations occur when reasoning and response generation exceed the allocated max_tokens (message.stop_reason == "max_tokens"). 1. First-Pass Truncation: If the initial budget max_tokens is less than ceiling, the system logs WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED_RETRY, logs the initial attempt's token usage, rebuilds the request parameters with max_tokens = ceiling, and re-invokes _send(). 2. Persistent Truncation: If the response remains truncated after the retry, or if the initial budget was already at ceiling, the system emits WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED and wraps the text in a TruncatedResponse(text) instance. Downstream cache layers detect this type and skip saving incomplete results.

docs.title: Server-Side Fallback Rejections
docs.text:
When requests include beta fallback headers on accounts or models that do not support them, the API raises anthropic.BadRequestError. The _send() helper catches this error and calls _fallback_rejected(). If the failure was caused by fallback beta restrictions: 

_fallbacks_disabled = True
emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED", error=str(e))
retry_params = {k: v for k, v in params.items() if k != "extra_body"}
return _stream_message(retry_params, [])
This disables fallback requests for the remainder of the session and immediately resends the stripped request, allowing the pipeline to proceed without interruption.

docs.title: Output Clamping Warnings
docs.text: During parameter resolution in _resolve_max_tokens(), if context window constraints or configuration caps reduce the planned generation budget by more than 10% (ceiling < wanted * 0.9), the system emits WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED to alert operators of potential capacity-driven truncations.

docs.title: llm_common.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/llm_common.py

Following the implementation of provider-specific transport engines such as llm_anthropic.py, llm_common.py serves as the shared, provider-neutral architectural foundation across all LLM backends in the system. It eliminates vendor lock-in and dependency bloat by relying exclusively on Python standard library modules (contextlib, contextvars, hashlib), purposefully avoiding imports from vendor SDKs such as google-genai or anthropic.

The module acts as the centralized accounting, memoization, and signaling layer for the entire inference pipeline. It maintains thread-safe and asynchronous task-safe step attribution using context variables, aggregates dual-ledger token and cost metrics across both providers and workflow execution steps, and persists deterministic request refusals to short-circuit wasteful API retries. Furthermore, it defines custom response markers and exception primitives that govern cache invalidation and retry semantics throughout upstream orchestration engines.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
llm_common.py implements four core operational capabilities required across all model interactions:

  1. Refusal Memoization: Large language models may decline requests due to safety guidelines, content filtering, or recitation checks. When an endpoint returns a deterministic, non-retryable refusal (such as a Claude policy refusal), continuing to retry the request within pipeline loops consumes rate limits and incurs billing penalties. llm_common.py maintains an in-memory SHA-256 digest mapping of refused requests via _refused, allowing subsequent attempts to immediately raise a cached LLMRefusalError without performing network I/O.
  2. Dual-Ledger Token and Cost Tracking: In-flight token consumption is categorized simultaneously across two dimensions: the LLM provider (e.g., Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter) and the workflow execution step (e.g., identify_abstractions, order_chapters). By utilizing a contextvars.ContextVar (_current_step), calls made deep within helper functions are automatically attributed to the active pipeline phase without requiring explicit parameter threading. The ledger tracks input, output, internal thinking tokens, prompt cache reads/writes, invocation counts, and micro-dollar API costs.
  3. Execution Diagnostics and Warning De-duplication: To prevent repetitive standard error output during long-running batch migrations or parallel node evaluations, the module provides a tuple-based deduplication mechanism (warn_once) that suppresses duplicate operational warnings.
  4. Flow Control Signaling: The module provides custom data structures such as TruncatedResponse to flag outputs that exceeded model token ceilings. This signals to downstream cache handlers that the response must not be written to disk, and informs orchestrator nodes that regeneration or context escalation is necessary.

docs.title: TruncatedResponse
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class TruncatedResponse(str):

Description: A specialized string subclass used to represent LLM generation text that was cut short by context length ceilings or max_tokens limits. By attaching the class attribute truncated = True, callers can treat the object as a regular string for logging while upstream orchestrators (such as call_llm.py or response parsers) can inspect the boolean flag to reject partial YAML/JSON schemas, bypass the on-disk LLM response cache, and trigger workflow retry policies.

Parameters: * Inherits standard str instantiation parameters.

Returns: * TruncatedResponse: An immutable string instance with .truncated set to True.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

class TruncatedResponse(str):
    """Response text from a reply that was cut off; call_llm returns it but never caches it."""

    truncated = True
The TruncatedResponse type provides transparent interoperability with standard string operations, allowing logging and text inspection without type coercion. However, because call_llm.py explicitly inspects isinstance(response, TruncatedResponse) or checks getattr(response, "truncated", False), responses wrapped in this class are prevented from poisoning the long-term cache (llm_cache_v2.json). Downstream parsers that encounter an unclosed JSON or YAML document utilize this flag to differentiate between malformed model syntax and hard token cutoffs.

docs.title: LLMRefusalError
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class LLMRefusalError(RuntimeError):

Description: Exception raised when a provider declines to answer a prompt due to policy enforcement, safety filtering, moderation violations, or recitation barriers. It carries operational metadata indicating the offending model, the specific refusal category, the originating provider, and a crucial retryable boolean flag.

Parameters: * model (str): The identifier of the model that refused the request. * category (str | None): The refusal reason reported by the provider (e.g., SAFETY, RECITATION, content_filter, or None). * provider (str, optional): The canonical provider name (defaults to "ANTHROPIC"). * retryable (bool, optional): Indicates whether a fresh generation attempt could bypass the refusal. Defaults to False.

Returns: * LLMRefusalError: Instantiated runtime exception.

Raises: * None during instantiation.

Example: 

class LLMRefusalError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the provider (and any configured fallback) declines a request."""

    def __init__(self, model: str, category: str | None, provider: str = "ANTHROPIC", retryable: bool = False):
        self.model = model
        self.category = category
        self.provider = provider
        self.retryable = retryable
        super().__init__(f"{provider} model {model} declined the request (category={category or 'unknown'})")
When retryable is False, the refusal is deterministic (for example, a system prompt containing prohibited strings), indicating that re-submitting the identical payload will produce another refusal. The calling harness registers these errors in llm_common's memoization dictionary to prevent repeated rate limit consumption. Conversely, when retryable is set to True (such as Gemini non-deterministic recitation blocks or output-side candidate safety filters), pipeline retry mechanisms are allowed to resample from the model.

docs.title: request_key()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def request_key(provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None, prompt: str) -> str:

Description: Generates a deterministic SHA-256 hash identifying a specific LLM invocation configuration and input payload. This hash serves as the lookup key in the refusal cache.

Parameters: * provider (str): The model host or gateway name (e.g., GEMINI, ANTHROPIC, OPENROUTER). * model (str): The specific model identifier (e.g., claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219). * thinking_level (str | None): The configured reasoning budget or effort level (e.g., low, medium, high, or None). * prompt (str): The complete serialized prompt text sent to the model.

Returns: * str: A 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def request_key(provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None, prompt: str) -> str:
    scope = f"{provider}|{model}|{(thinking_level or 'default').lower()}\n"
    return hashlib.sha256((scope + prompt).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
The hashing strategy incorporates the provider, model, normalized thinking level, and prompt into a single scoped string before computing the SHA-256 digest. By converting thinking_level to lowercase and falling back to "default", variations in parameter casing are normalized. This ensures that memoized refusals are accurately bound to identical runtime configurations, preventing false cache hits across differing models or reasoning depths.

docs.title: remember_refusal()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def remember_refusal(key: str, error: LLMRefusalError) -> None:

Description: Stores an LLMRefusalError instance in the internal process-level refusal registry keyed by its request hash digest.

Parameters: * key (str): The 64-character SHA-256 string generated by request_key(). * error (LLMRefusalError): The refusal exception instance to record.

Returns: * None

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def remember_refusal(key: str, error: LLMRefusalError) -> None:
    _refused[key] = error
This function populates the private _refused dictionary. It is invoked by calling gateways (e.g., call_llm.py) immediately upon trapping a non-retryable refusal from any downstream provider adapter. Storing the complete exception instance ensures that the original error context, category, and provider details are preserved for subsequent lookup.

docs.title: previous_refusal()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def previous_refusal(key: str) -> LLMRefusalError | None:

Description: Queries the process-level refusal registry to check if an identical request configuration has previously resulted in a refusal.

Parameters: * key (str): The 64-character SHA-256 string generated by request_key().

Returns: * LLMRefusalError | None: The cached refusal exception if a prior decline exists; otherwise None.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def previous_refusal(key: str) -> LLMRefusalError | None:
    return _refused.get(key)
Before dispatching a network call to any provider, orchestrators pass the request key through this function. If an LLMRefusalError is returned, the caller re-raises it immediately. This prevents unnecessary network round-trips and protects API quota when downstream pipeline nodes execute automated retry attempts on deterministic failures.

docs.title: usage_step()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def usage_step(step: str | None):

Description: A context manager that scopes all token usage and event logging executed within its context block to a named workflow pipeline step.

Parameters: * step (str | None): The identifier of the workflow step (e.g., identify_abstractions, order_chapters, group_modules). If None or empty, defaults to "other".

Returns: * Context manager generator yielding execution control.

Raises: * None directly; preserves and propagates exceptions raised within the wrapped block.

Example: 

@contextlib.contextmanager
def usage_step(step: str | None):
    """Attribute every record_usage / count_event inside the block to `step`."""
    token = _current_step.set(step or "other")
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        _current_step.reset(token)
The context manager leverages Python's contextvars.ContextVar to manage step context. When entering the block, it assigns the step identifier to _current_step and stores the resulting reset token. Inside the finally block, it restores the previous context variable state using _current_step.reset(token). This structure guarantees accurate step attribution even across deeply nested generator flows, exception bubbles, or asynchronous task boundaries.

docs.title: current_step()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def current_step() -> str:

Description: Retrieves the active workflow step identifier from the execution context.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * str: The active step name set by the surrounding usage_step() context, or "other" if called outside of a scoped block.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def current_step() -> str:
    return _current_step.get()
This utility function inspects _current_step to allow accounting functions (such as record_usage, count_event, and record_estimate) to automatically determine which workflow subtotal should be credited without requiring callers to pass the step name down the call stack.

docs.title: record_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: 

def record_usage(
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    *,
    input_tokens: int = 0,
    output_tokens: int = 0,
    thinking_tokens: int = 0,
    cache_read: int = 0,
    cache_write: int = 0,
    cost: float | None = None,
    measured: bool = True,
) -> None:

Description: Accumulates token consumption, cache performance metrics, and financial costs for an API request into both the provider-level ledger and the current step ledger.

Parameters: * provider (str): Target provider name (e.g., "GEMINI", "ANTHROPIC"). * model (str): Target model name. If non-empty, it is registered in the entry's model tracking set. * input_tokens (int, optional): Total prompt tokens counted by the provider, including cached tokens. Defaults to 0. * output_tokens (int, optional): Total output tokens returned, including reasoning/thinking tokens. Defaults to 0. * thinking_tokens (int, optional): Explicit reasoning or thinking tokens reported by the provider. Defaults to 0. * cache_read (int, optional): Subset of prompt tokens retrieved from provider-side prompt cache. Defaults to 0. * cache_write (int, optional): Subset of prompt tokens written to provider-side prompt cache. Defaults to 0. * cost (float | None, optional): Financial cost of the call in USD. If None, the call is marked as unpriced. * measured (bool, optional): Whether the provider returned verified usage metrics. When False, increments unmeasured_calls. Defaults to True.

Returns: * None

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def record_usage(
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    *,
    input_tokens: int = 0,
    output_tokens: int = 0,
    thinking_tokens: int = 0,
    cache_read: int = 0,
    cache_write: int = 0,
    cost: float | None = None,
    measured: bool = True,
) -> None:
    for entry in (_usage.setdefault(provider, _new_entry()), _steps.setdefault(current_step(), _new_entry())):
        if model:
            entry["models"].add(model)
        entry["calls"] += 1
        if not measured:
            entry["unmeasured_calls"] += 1
        entry["input"] += input_tokens or 0
        entry["output"] += output_tokens or 0
        entry["thinking"] += thinking_tokens or 0
        entry["cache_read"] += cache_read or 0
        entry["cache_write"] += cache_write or 0
        if cost is None:
            entry["unpriced_calls"] += 1
        else:
            entry["cost"] += cost
record_usage updates two distinct tracking dictionaries simultaneously: _usage (partitioned by provider) and _steps (partitioned by the active context step). Safe integer coercion via or 0 ensures that None values passed by upstream provider adapters do not cause TypeError exceptions during arithmetic accumulation. If cost is None, the unpriced_calls counter is incremented, signaling to downstream reporting summaries that the financial total represents an incomplete minimum lower bound.

docs.title: count_event()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def count_event(provider: str, event: str) -> None:

Description: Increments designated lifecycle event counters ("refusals", "fallbacks", or "truncations") for both the provider and the active execution step.

Parameters: * provider (str): Target provider name. * event (str): The metric key to increment. Must be one of "refusals", "fallbacks", or "truncations".

Returns: * None

Raises: * KeyError: If event is not a valid key defined in _new_entry().

Example: 

def count_event(provider: str, event: str) -> None:
    """Increment 'refusals' | 'fallbacks' | 'truncations' for a provider (and the current step)."""
    _usage.setdefault(provider, _new_entry())[event] += 1
    _steps.setdefault(current_step(), _new_entry())[event] += 1
This function provides a lightweight telemetry interface for tracking runtime occurrences that do not produce standard token responses. For example, when llm_anthropic.py recovers from a context limit error by activating server-side fallback flags, or when call_llm.py encounters a model truncation, invoking count_event() ensures these events are tracked across both provider summaries and pipeline step reports.

docs.title: record_estimate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def record_estimate(step: str, estimated_input: int, *, cache_hit: bool = False) -> None:

Description: Records pre-flight token estimates or local cache hit events for a given workflow step.

Parameters: * step (str): The name of the pipeline step being measured. * estimated_input (int): The locally calculated input token estimate (e.g., derived via tiktoken). * cache_hit (bool, optional): Indicates whether the request was satisfied by the local cache (llm_cache_v2.json) without making a network call. Defaults to False.

Returns: * None

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def record_estimate(step: str, estimated_input: int, *, cache_hit: bool = False) -> None:
    """Add call_llm's input estimate for a call (billed or served from the LLM cache) to a step."""
    entry = _steps.setdefault(step or "other", _new_entry())
    if cache_hit:
        entry["cache_hits"] += 1
    else:
        entry["estimated_input"] += estimated_input or 0
This function enables token budgeting calibration. When a request is served entirely from the local cache, incrementing cache_hits ensures the step summary accounts for avoided API requests. When a network call is required, accumulating estimated_input allows the system to evaluate estimation drift against the actual provider-billed input metrics.

docs.title: usage_snapshot()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def usage_snapshot(provider: str) -> dict:

Description: Creates a point-in-time copy of a provider's numeric usage counters, omitting non-scalar values such as model sets.

Parameters: * provider (str): The provider whose metrics should be captured.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary mapping metric names to their current integer or float values.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def usage_snapshot(provider: str) -> dict:
    """Copy of a provider's running totals (diff two snapshots to get one call's usage)."""
    entry = _usage.get(provider)
    return {k: v for k, v in entry.items() if k != "models"} if entry else {k: v for k, v in _new_entry().items() if k != "models"}
By excluding the "models" set, usage_snapshot() returns a snapshot of purely numeric fields. This dictionary is designed to be passed into usage_delta() to isolate the specific token usage and cost incurred during a single network call.

docs.title: usage_delta()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def usage_delta(before: dict, after: dict) -> dict:

Description: Computes the difference between two usage snapshot dictionaries.

Parameters: * before (dict): The baseline snapshot taken before executing the operation. * after (dict): The snapshot taken after completing the operation.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing the net change (after[k] - before[k]) for every counter key.

Raises: * KeyError: If a key present in after is missing from before and lacks a fallback default.

Example: 

def usage_delta(before: dict, after: dict) -> dict:
    return {k: after[k] - before.get(k, 0) for k in after}
This utility calculates exact per-call resource consumption. Because client SDKs and streaming interfaces may execute internal retries or multi-segment reasoning loops, calculating the delta across cumulative snapshots reliably captures total consumption, regardless of internal transport behavior.

docs.title: get_usage_summary()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_usage_summary() -> dict:

Description: Compiles a summary dictionary of usage statistics for every provider that executed at least one API call during the current process run.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * dict: A mapping of provider names to public summary dictionaries (see Data Structures).

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def get_usage_summary() -> dict:
    """{provider: totals} for every provider that made at least one call this run."""
    return {provider: _public(entry) for provider, entry in _usage.items() if entry["calls"]}
Providers that were configured or initialized but made no API requests (entry["calls"] == 0) are filtered out of the summary. For active providers, internal entries are converted to public representations using _public(), sorting model sets into lists and determining price completeness flags.

docs.title: get_step_summary()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_step_summary() -> dict:

Description: Compiles a summary dictionary of usage statistics partitioned by workflow step, ordered by first appearance.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * dict: A mapping of step identifiers to public summary dictionaries (see Data Structures).

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def get_step_summary() -> dict:
    """{step: totals} in first-use order, including steps answered only from the LLM cache."""
    return {step: _public(entry) for step, entry in _steps.items() if entry["calls"] or entry["cache_hits"]}
get_step_summary() retains insertion ordering based on when steps were first registered during execution. Unlike provider summaries, steps are included if they made direct API calls or were satisfied by local cache hits (entry["calls"] or entry["cache_hits"]). This ensures that cached steps are accurately reflected in end-of-run execution metrics.

docs.title: reset_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def reset_usage() -> None:

Description: Clears all internal tracking state, resetting provider ledgers, step breakdowns, and the refusal cache.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * None

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def reset_usage() -> None:
    _usage.clear()
    _steps.clear()
    _refused.clear()
This function resets state between independent test suites or workflow executions within long-lived processes. It purges the _usage, _steps, and _refused dictionaries. Note that _warned is preserved to prevent duplicate warnings from re-appearing across soft resets.

docs.title: warn_once()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def warn_once(key: str, *parts) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether a warning identified by a composite key tuple has been emitted during the lifetime of the process.

Parameters: * key (str): The primary identifier or category of the warning. * *parts (Any): Additional elements combined with key to form a composite identity tuple.

Returns: * bool: True if this is the first time the composite key has been seen; False if it has already been observed.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def warn_once(key: str, *parts) -> bool:
    """True the first time a (key, parts) combination is seen this run."""
    marker = (key, *parts)
    if marker in _warned:
        return False
    _warned.add(marker)
    return True
Callers use warn_once within diagnostic logging branches to guard against log flooding. By checking the return value before emitting output via utils.output, warning messages are logged only on their initial occurrence, suppressing repetitive notices across batch processing loops.

docs.title: _new_entry()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _new_entry() -> dict:

Description: Factory function that creates and returns a zero-initialized usage ledger entry dictionary.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing baseline metric counters and an empty model tracking set.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def _new_entry() -> dict:
    return {
        "models": set(),
        "calls": 0,
        "input": 0,
        "output": 0,
        "thinking": 0,
        "cache_read": 0,
        "cache_write": 0,
        "cost": 0.0,
        "unpriced_calls": 0,
        "unmeasured_calls": 0,
        "refusals": 0,
        "fallbacks": 0,
        "truncations": 0,
        "estimated_input": 0,
        "cache_hits": 0,
    }
This helper defines the structural schema for both the provider ledger (_usage) and the workflow step ledger (_steps). Initializing models as an empty set ensures deduplicated tracking of all model variants encountered by a provider or pipeline phase.

docs.title: _public()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _public(entry: dict) -> dict:

Description: Formats an internal ledger entry dictionary into an external summary representation suitable for serialization and telemetry reporting.

Parameters: * entry (dict): An internal ledger entry created via _new_entry().

Returns: * dict: A copy of entry with "models" converted from a set to a sorted list, and a computed "cost_known" boolean indicating whether all calls were priced.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def _public(entry: dict) -> dict:
    return dict(entry, models=sorted(entry["models"]), cost_known=entry["unpriced_calls"] == 0)
Internal ledger entries use Python set objects to track unique model identifiers, which cannot be directly serialized to JSON. _public transforms this set into a sorted list of strings. It also computes cost_known, which evaluates to True only when unpriced_calls == 0, signaling whether the accumulated cost represents a complete total or an incomplete estimate.

docs.title: Internal Ledger Entry (_new_entry)
docs.text:
The schema used internally to aggregate metrics within _usage and _steps.

Field Type Description models set[str] Set of unique model identifiers that handled requests. calls int Total number of API requests dispatched. input int Total prompt tokens reported by the provider (cached tokens included). output int Total output tokens returned (including reasoning tokens). thinking int Subset of output tokens dedicated to internal reasoning/thinking. cache_read int Subset of prompt tokens read from provider-side prompt cache. cache_write int Subset of prompt tokens written to provider-side prompt cache. cost float Cumulative financial cost calculated in USD. unpriced_calls int Count of requests where pricing models were unavailable (cost is None). unmeasured_calls int Count of calls where the provider returned no token usage metrics. refusals int Number of times requests were rejected by provider safety or policy checks. fallbacks int Number of times fallback configurations or beta overrides were invoked. truncations int Number of times response generations reached token limits. estimated_input int Pre-calculated prompt token estimates derived prior to invocation. cache_hits int Number of requests satisfied by the local cache without network calls.

docs.title: Public Summary Entry (_public)
docs.text:
The transformed schema returned by get_usage_summary() and get_step_summary().

Field Type Description models list[str] Alphabetically sorted list of all model names used. calls int Total number of API requests dispatched. input int Total prompt tokens counted across calls. output int Total output tokens generated. thinking int Total thinking/reasoning tokens generated. cache_read int Total prompt cache read tokens. cache_write int Total prompt cache write tokens. cost float Cumulative calculated cost in USD. cost_known bool True if every call was priced (unpriced_calls == 0); False otherwise. unpriced_calls int Number of calls lacking explicit pricing. unmeasured_calls int Number of unmeasured calls. refusals int Total provider refusal count. fallbacks int Total provider fallback count. truncations int Total truncated response count. estimated_input int Total estimated prompt tokens. cache_hits int Total requests answered from the local cache.

docs.title: Non-Retryable Refusal Memoization
docs.text:
Deterministic provider refusals pose a risk in automated pipelines with retry policies. For instance, if an input violates safety restrictions or triggers recitation filters, naive retries will repeatedly fail, consuming rate limits and increasing latency.

llm_common.py resolves this using the following pattern: 1. call_llm.py computes a hash via request_key(provider, model, thinking_level, prompt). 2. It queries previous_refusal(key). If an entry exists and error.retryable is False, the cached exception is immediately raised without initiating a network request. 3. If an endpoint rejects an active request, the provider adapter raises LLMRefusalError(..., retryable=False). 4. Upstream catch handlers invoke remember_refusal(key, err) and record the event via count_event(provider, 'refusals').

docs.title: Truncation Signaling without Disk Poisoning
docs.text: When an LLM exhausts its max_tokens allocation or context window, returning a partially formed response can cause downstream JSON/YAML parsing errors. Rather than raising an immediate unrecoverable exception, llm_common.py defines TruncatedResponse: * Adapters wrap truncated output strings in TruncatedResponse(raw_text). * call_llm.py inspects isinstance(result, TruncatedResponse) and bypasses writing the incomplete response to llm_cache_v2.json. * Downstream orchestration nodes receive the response, evaluate its .truncated attribute, and can trigger context window escalation or prompt compression before retrying.

docs.title: Unpriced and Unmeasured Safety Fallbacks
docs.text: Pricing configurations may not cover every experimental or locally hosted model (e.g., custom Ollama checkpoints). When a request's pricing cannot be resolved: * record_usage() accepts cost=None, tracks the call, and increments unpriced_calls. * When reporting summaries via _public(), cost_known evaluates to False. This warns operators that the reported cost total represents an incomplete floor rather than a definitive invoice total. * When endpoints return zero token metrics or omit usage headers entirely, setting measured=False tracks the call count while isolating the entry from token calibration metrics via unmeasured_calls.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• call_llm.py — Central routing gateway that imports TruncatedResponse, LLMRefusalError, and ledger tracking utilities to coordinate LLM execution.
  • llm_anthropic.py — Anthropic Claude provider adapter that reports token usage and manages reasoning budgets through llm_common.
  • llm_gemini.py — Google Gemini provider adapter that maps candidate safety blocks to LLMRefusalError and records usage metrics.
  • llm_openrouter.py — OpenRouter adapter handling moderation rejections and variable pricing schemas recorded in the common ledger.
  • token_utils.py — Estimation utilities that calculate input token ratios compared against record_estimate().
  • output.py — Telemetry emitter responsible for rendering formatted usage tables generated by get_usage_summary() and get_step_summary().

docs.title: llm_config.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/llm_config.py

Following the centralized accounting and ledger mechanisms established in llm_common.py, llm_config.py acts as the foundational model configuration, credential preflight, and context-length resolution engine. It resolves circular dependencies across the codebase by serving as the decoupled single source of truth for runtime provider settings, budget calculations, and model parameter adaptation.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The llm_config.py module establishes the configuration baseline and operational constraints for all Large Language Model (LLM) interactions across the system. Historically coupled within the invocation pipeline, this component was extracted from call_llm.py to break an architectural circular dependency between model dispatching and token budgeting in token_utils.py. By centralizing configuration parsing, environment resolution, and provider inspection into a standalone utility, both orchestration modules and downstream transport harnesses can query runtime parameters without initiating circular imports or eager SDK instantiations.

The module provides deterministic resolution mechanisms across four distinct provider domains: Google Gemini (both AI Studio and Vertex AI endpoints), Anthropic Claude (supporting direct API keys, authentication tokens, Workload Identity Federation, and native ant auth CLI sessions), OpenRouter (with real-time catalog lookups and routing suffix normalization), and generic OpenAI-compatible custom endpoints. In addition to credentials, llm_config.py standardizes provider-specific thinking regimes, token sizing multipliers (bridging discrepancies between cl100k_base tiktoken estimates and native model tokenizers), and output limits.

The preflight validation pipeline implemented by this module intercepts configuration deficiencies before resource-intensive repository crawling or multi-phase graph workflows begin. It inspects local Python environment dependencies (such as ensuring google-genai meets minimum semantic version thresholds), probes active CLI authentication states via subprocess wrappers, queries remote provider model catalogs with automatic failure cooldowns, and cross-references requested models against retirement or deprecation matrices.
