docs.title: write_mkdocs_output()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def write_mkdocs_output(output_path, prep_res, chapter_files) -> None:

Description: Orchestrates the complete compilation and file system serialization of an MkDocs documentation site. It resolves navigation trees, executes optional LLM section clustering, creates directories, generates mkdocs.yml, injects frontend helper scripts, normalizes inter-chapter hyperlinking, and persists all generated chapter markdown files.

Parameters: * output_path (str): Target base directory on the local filesystem where the documentation site is compiled. * prep_res (dict): Upstream pipeline state containing project metadata, execution mode, language preferences, directory trees, token budgets, and fallback navigation snippets. * chapter_files (list[dict]): Collection of chapter dictionaries containing module names, relative paths, filenames, descriptions, and markdown body content.

Returns: * None: Writes files directly to the filesystem.

Raises: * OSError: If directory creation or file writing fails due to filesystem permissions or disk constraints.

docs.title: Phase 1: Output Path Initialization and Mode Labeling
docs.text:
project_name = prep_res["project_name"]
    mode = prep_res["mode"]
    api_docs_path = os.path.join(output_path, "docs", "api")
    os.makedirs(api_docs_path, exist_ok=True)

    mode_labels = {
        "tutorial": get("UI_MODE_TUTORIAL"),
        "advanced": get("UI_MODE_ADVANCED"),
        "sdk": get("UI_MODE_SDK"),
        "api-reference": get("UI_MODE_API_REF"),
    }
    site_title = f"{project_name} — {mode_labels.get(mode, 'Documentation')}"
    emit("COMBINE_FORMAT_MKDOCS", mode=mode_labels.get(mode, "Documentation"))
    emit("COMBINE_CHAPTER_COUNT", count=len(chapter_files))
This initial phase resolves the documentation mode and establishes the directory layout. It ensures the nested API output directory (docs/api/) exists using os.makedirs. It maps raw mode identifiers to localized UI display names using get(), constructs the overarching site title string, and broadcasts progress notifications to the event telemetry stream.

docs.title: Phase 2: Dynamic LLM Navigation Grouping
docs.text:
# --- LLM-Assisted Nav Grouping (api-reference only, 6+ modules) ---
    sections = None
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"NAV GROUPING CHECK | mode={mode} | module_count={len(chapter_files)} | threshold=6", dest="LOG")
    if mode == "api-reference" and len(chapter_files) > 5:
        try:
            chapter_summaries = prep_res.get("chapter_summaries", [])
            module_entries = []
            for i, cf in enumerate(chapter_files):
                summary = chapter_summaries[i] if i < len(chapter_summaries) and chapter_summaries[i] else cf["description"]
                module_entries.append(f"- {cf['module_name']}: {summary}")
            module_list = "\n".join(module_entries)

            # Load grouping prompt template
            prompt_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "prompts", "common", "group_modules.md")
            with open(prompt_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                group_template = f.read()

            language = prep_res.get("language", "english")
            language_note = f"Section names MUST be in {language}." if language.lower() != "english" else ""

            group_prompt = group_template.format(
                project_name=project_name,
                module_count=len(chapter_files),
                module_list=module_list,
                directory_tree=prep_res.get("directory_tree", "N/A"),
                language_note=language_note,
            )

            emit("LLM_CALL_GROUPING", count=len(chapter_files))

            log_token_estimation("NavGrouping", group_prompt, prep_res.get("max_tokens", 100000))
            group_response = call_llm(
                group_prompt, use_cache=prep_res.get("use_cache", True), thinking_level=prep_res.get("thinking_level"), step="group_modules"
            )
            parsed = parse_yaml_response(group_response)
            sections = parsed.get("sections", parsed) if isinstance(parsed, dict) else None
            # ...
For API reference documentation containing six or more modules, this phase invokes an LLM to categorize disparate code files into functional domains. It formats module names, descriptions, and the physical directory tree into the group_modules.md prompt template. The prompt enforces output localization matching the target language, calculates token estimation metrics via log_token_estimation(), and executes inference through call_llm(), parsing the resulting YAML hierarchy into structured section nodes.

docs.title: Phase 3: Navigation Fallback and Assembly
docs.text:
if sections:
                # Validate: ensure all modules are covered
                grouped_modules = collect_all_modules(sections)
                ungrouped = [cf["module_name"] for cf in chapter_files if cf["module_name"] not in grouped_modules]
                if ungrouped:
                    sections.append({"name": get("UI_OTHER"), "modules": ungrouped})

                nav_lines = build_grouped_nav(sections, chapter_files, indent=4)
                nav_lines.insert(0, "    - api/index.md")
                nav_label = mode_labels.get(mode, "Documentation")
                nav_snippet = f"nav:\n  - {nav_label}:\n" + "\n".join(nav_lines)
                emit("DONE_GROUPING", count=len(sections))
            else:
                emit("GROUP_EMPTY_FALLBACK")
                nav_snippet = prep_res["nav_snippet"]

        except Exception as e:
            emit("GROUP_ERROR_FALLBACK", error=e)
            emit_raw("ERROR", f"LLM grouping failed: {e}\n{traceback.format_exc()}", dest="LOG")
            nav_snippet = prep_res["nav_snippet"]
            sections = None
    else:
        nav_snippet = prep_res["nav_snippet"]
This phase validates the section hierarchy produced by the LLM. It computes the difference between total known modules and grouped modules via collect_all_modules(), defensively appending any missed modules into an "Other" category. If parsing fails, returns empty sections, or encounters network exceptions, it logs the stack trace and falls back to the deterministic flat navigation tree stored in prep_res["nav_snippet"].

docs.title: Phase 4: MkDocs Configuration and Static Assets Generation
docs.text:
# --- Generate mkdocs.yml ---
    lang_code_map = {
        "vietnamese": "vi",
        "chinese": "zh",
        "japanese": "ja",
        "korean": "ko",
        "french": "fr",
        "spanish": "es",
        "german": "de",
        "portuguese": "pt",
        "russian": "ru",
        "thai": "th",
        "indonesian": "id",
        "arabic": "ar",
    }
    language = prep_res.get("language", "english")
    lang_code = lang_code_map.get(language.lower(), "")
    mkdocs_config = build_mkdocs_config(site_title, nav_snippet, include_home=True, lang_code=lang_code)
    mkdocs_filepath = os.path.join(output_path, "mkdocs.yml")
    with open(mkdocs_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(mkdocs_config)
    emit("FILE_WROTE", path=mkdocs_filepath)

    # --- Generate javascripts/mermaid-init.js ---
    js_dir = os.path.join(output_path, "docs", "javascripts")
    os.makedirs(js_dir, exist_ok=True)
    js_filepath = os.path.join(js_dir, "mermaid-init.js")
    with open(js_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(build_mermaid_init_js())
    emit("FILE_WROTE", path=js_filepath)
This phase synthesizes the site configuration and static script assets. It resolves the appropriate two-letter ISO language code for the Material theme, serializes the complete mkdocs.yml configuration string, and writes it to the output root. It also initializes the docs/javascripts/ directory and writes mermaid-init.js, ensuring interactive client-side diagram rendering operates properly.

docs.title: Phase 5: Index Assembly, Link Normalization, and Chapter Persistence
docs.text:
# --- Generate docs/index.md — homepage redirect to api/ ---
    mode_label = mode_labels.get(mode, "Documentation")
    home_index_path = os.path.join(output_path, "docs", "index.md")
    home_content = f'# {project_name}\n\n<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; url=api/">\n\n[→ {mode_label}](api/index.md)\n'
    with open(home_index_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(home_content)
    emit("FILE_WROTE", path=home_index_path)

    # ... [Build docs/api/index.md table and write nav_snippet.yml] ...

    # --- Normalize cross-chapter links ---
    normalize_chapter_links(chapter_files)

    # --- Write chapter files ---
    for chapter_info in chapter_files:
        chapter_filepath = os.path.join(api_docs_path, chapter_info["filename"])
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(chapter_filepath), exist_ok=True)
        with open(chapter_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(chapter_info["content"])
        emit("FILE_WROTE", path=chapter_filepath)
In the final phase, the root landing page docs/index.md is compiled with an instant HTTP meta-refresh redirect pointing to api/. The module then builds the detailed index catalog at docs/api/index.md, serializes the raw navigation tree to docs/nav_snippet.yml, executes in-place Markdown link target normalization via normalize_chapter_links(), and writes every chapter file to disk, creating nested directories as required.

Example: 

# Invocation of write_mkdocs_output inside workflow execution nodes:
write_mkdocs_output(
    output_path=output_dir,
    prep_res={
        "project_name": "SampleProject",
        "mode": "api-reference",
        "language": "english",
        "nav_snippet": "nav:\n  - API: api/index.md",
    },
    chapter_files=chapters,
)

docs.title: write_standalone_output()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def write_standalone_output(output_path, prep_res, chapter_files, ui) -> None:

Description: Persists documentation content in a standalone Markdown structure without generating an MkDocs Material site. It generates a top-level index.md, writes individual chapter files directly into the root destination folder, and concatenates all chapters into a single monolithic full_content.md document complete with internal HTML anchor targets and a table of contents.

Parameters: * output_path (str): Local filesystem directory where markdown deliverables are created. * prep_res (dict): Upstream pipeline state containing pre-rendered index_content. * chapter_files (list[dict]): Collection of chapter dictionaries containing filenames, titles, and body content. * ui (dict): UI localization strings containing translated labels for "toc" and "chapter".

Returns: * None: Writes files directly to disk.

Raises: * OSError: If writing to the destination directory fails due to system I/O errors.

docs.title: Phase 1: Table of Contents and Chapter Serialization
docs.text:
index_content = prep_res["index_content"]
    emit("COMBINE_FORMAT_STANDALONE")
    emit("COMBINE_CHAPTER_COUNT", count=len(chapter_files))

    # Write index.md
    index_filepath = os.path.join(output_path, "index.md")
    with open(index_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(index_content)
    emit("FILE_WROTE", path=index_filepath)

    # Write chapter files
    for chapter_info in chapter_files:
        chapter_filepath = os.path.join(output_path, chapter_info["filename"])
        with open(chapter_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(chapter_info["content"])
        emit("FILE_WROTE", path=chapter_filepath)
This phase records telemetry indicating standalone formatting and writes the primary summary catalog index.md from prep_res["index_content"]. It then iterates through chapter_files, persisting each markdown chapter directly under output_path using UTF-8 encoding.

docs.title: Phase 2: Full Content Concatenation (full_content.md)
docs.text:
# Create full_content.md
    toc_lines = [f"# {ui['toc']}\n"]
    full_content_lines = []

    for i, chapter_info in enumerate(chapter_files):
        content = chapter_info["content"]
        title_line = content.split("\n", 1)[0]
        if title_line.startswith("# "):
            title = title_line[2:].strip()
        else:
            title = f"{ui['chapter']} {i + 1}"

        toc_lines.append(f"- [{title}](#chapter-{i + 1})")
        full_content_lines.append(f'<a id="chapter-{i + 1}"></a>\n')
        full_content_lines.append(content)
        full_content_lines.append("\n---\n")

    full_content = "\n".join(toc_lines) + "\n\n" + "\n".join(full_content_lines)
    full_content_filepath = os.path.join(output_path, "full_content.md")
    with open(full_content_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(full_content)
    emit("FILE_WROTE", path=full_content_filepath)
This phase iterates through all chapters to assemble a single unified markdown document. It extracts each chapter's top-level heading (# Title) to construct an introductory Table of Contents list linking to internal HTML anchors (#chapter-N). It appends each chapter separated by an HTML anchor (<a id="chapter-N"></a>) and a thematic divider (---), serializing the consolidated payload to full_content.md.

Example: 

# Standalone invocation for offline single-file reading
ui_strings = {"toc": "Table of Contents", "chapter": "Chapter"}
write_standalone_output("/path/to/dist", prep_data, chapters, ui_strings)

docs.title: build_mkdocs_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_mkdocs_config(site_name: str, nav_yaml: str, include_home: bool = True, lang_code: str = "") -> str:

Description: Constructs the complete, valid YAML contents of an mkdocs.yml configuration file configured for Material for MkDocs. Configures code block copy buttons, PyMdown Extensions syntax highlighting, inline highlighting, panzoom integration, custom superfences for Mermaid diagrams, optional theme localization, and navigation structures.

Parameters: * site_name (str): Display title of the documentation project. * nav_yaml (str): Pre-formatted YAML string containing navigation entries. * include_home (bool, optional): Whether to inject a root Home: index.md navigation entry. Defaults to True. * lang_code (str, optional): Two-letter ISO language code (e.g., "vi", "zh", "fr") to localize theme elements. Defaults to "".

Returns: * str: Fully formatted mkdocs.yml configuration string.

Raises: * None.

def build_mkdocs_config(site_name: str, nav_yaml: str, include_home: bool = True, lang_code: str = "") -> str:
    # Extract nav items from nav_snippet (strip the "nav:" header line)
    nav_lines = nav_yaml.split("\n")
    nav_body = "\n".join(nav_lines[1:]) if nav_lines else ""

    # Conditional Home nav entry (CI has root index.md, local mkdocs doesn't)
    home_line = "  - Home: index.md\n" if include_home else ""

    # Optional Material theme language (e.g. "vi", "zh", "ja", "ko")
    lang_line = f"  language: {lang_code}\n" if lang_code else ""

    return (
        f"site_name: {yaml_str(site_name)}\n"
        f"theme:\n"
        f"  name: material\n"
        f"{lang_line}"
        f"  features:\n"
        f"    - content.code.copy\n"
        f"    - navigation.indexes\n"
        f"  palette:\n"
        f"    - scheme: default\n"
        f"      toggle:\n"
        f"        icon: material/brightness-7\n"
        f"        name: Switch to dark mode\n"
        f"    - scheme: slate\n"
        f"      toggle:\n"
        f"        icon: material/brightness-4\n"
        f"        name: Switch to light mode\n"
        f"plugins:\n"
        f"  - search\n"
        f"  - panzoom:\n"
        f"      include_selectors:\n"
        f"        - '.mermaid-raw'\n"
        f"markdown_extensions:\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.highlight:\n"
        f"      anchor_linenums: true\n"
        f"      use_pygments: true\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.superfences:\n"
        f"      custom_fences:\n"
        f"        - name: mermaid\n"
        f"          class: mermaid-raw\n"
        f"          format: !!python/name:pymdownx.superfences.fence_code_format\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.inlinehilite\n"
        f"extra_javascript:\n"
        f"  - https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11/dist/mermaid.min.js\n"
        f"  - javascripts/mermaid-init.js\n"
        f"nav:\n"
        f"{home_line}"
        f"{nav_body}\n"
    )
The function strips the leading nav: header from nav_yaml to prevent invalid duplicate top-level keys when nesting the navigation body. It attaches the panzoom plugin configured to target the .mermaid-raw selector and registers pymdownx.superfences using fence_code_format with the mermaid-raw CSS class. This configuration prevents Material for MkDocs from applying theme-level CSS overrides to diagrams, delegating rendering to the external Mermaid 11 library and javascripts/mermaid-init.js.

Example: 

config_text = build_mkdocs_config(
    site_name="Knowledge Core",
    nav_yaml="nav:\n  - Overview: api/index.md",
    include_home=True,
    lang_code="vi"
)

docs.title: yaml_str()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def yaml_str(value) -> str:

Description: Sanitizes and quotes a scalar string for direct interpolation into hand-built YAML documents. It leverages json.dumps with ensure_ascii=False to produce double-quoted string literals that strictly adhere to YAML 1.2 scalar specifications, preventing parsing errors from colons, apostrophes, square brackets, leading @ symbols, or non-ASCII Unicode characters.

Parameters: * value (Any): Scalar object or string to quote.

Returns: * str: JSON double-quoted string valid in YAML scalar positions.

Raises: * None.

def yaml_str(value) -> str:
    """Quote a scalar for hand-built YAML (nav labels, section names, titles).

    JSON string literals are valid YAML double-quoted scalars, so names containing
    apostrophes, colons, brackets or a leading @ never break mkdocs.yml or frontmatter.
    """
    return json.dumps(str(value).strip(), ensure_ascii=False)
By delegating to json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False), the function wraps input text in standard double quotes, safely escapes interior double quotes (\") and newline controls (\n), and preserves UTF-8 characters verbatim. This ensures that module paths and arbitrary project names containing special punctuation can be injected into mkdocs.yml without generating malformed syntax.

Example: 

# Quoting a module name with colons or special characters
safe_label = yaml_str("Service: Core [v2]")
# safe_label evaluates to: '"Service: Core [v2]"'

docs.title: build_grouped_nav()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def build_grouped_nav(sections: list, chapter_files: list, indent: int = 4) -> list[str]:

Description: Recursively compiles a list of formatted YAML lines representing the MkDocs navigation hierarchy from LLM-generated section structures. Handles arbitrary tree depth via nested children nodes and matches module names against chapter_files. Modules residing in nested subdirectories are grouped under deterministic directory sub-layers, whereas root-level files remain flat.

Parameters: * sections (list[dict]): Tree of section definitions, where each node contains "name", an optional list of "modules", and optional nested "children". * chapter_files (list[dict]): Collection of chapter metadata records containing module_name, original_path, and filename. * indent (int, optional): Indentation whitespace count for the current tree depth. Defaults to 4.

Returns: * list[str]: Sequence of indented YAML navigation lines.

Raises: * None.

def build_grouped_nav(sections: list, chapter_files: list, indent: int = 4) -> list[str]:
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"build_grouped_nav | building nav for {len(sections)} sections", dest="LOG")

    lines = []
    pad = " " * indent
    for section in sections:
        lines.append(f"{pad}- {yaml_str(section['name'])}:")
        if "children" in section:
            lines.extend(build_grouped_nav(section["children"], chapter_files, indent + 2))

        # Collect matched modules with directory info
        matched = []
        for mod_name in section.get("modules", []):
            match = next((cf for cf in chapter_files if cf["module_name"] == mod_name), None)
            if match:
                dir_path = os.path.dirname(match.get("original_path", "")) or ""
                matched.append((dir_path, mod_name, match))

        # Group by directory
        dir_groups = defaultdict(list)
        for dir_path, mod_name, match in matched:
            dir_groups[dir_path].append((mod_name, match))

        # Emit dir sub-layers for non-root dirs, flat for root files
        has_non_root = any(d for d in dir_groups)
        if has_non_root:
            for dir_path in sorted(dir_groups.keys()):
                if dir_path:
                    # Non-root: add directory sub-layer with bare module names
                    lines.append(f"{pad}  - {yaml_str(dir_path)}:")
                    for mod_name, match in dir_groups[dir_path]:
                        lines.append(f"{pad}    - {yaml_str(mod_name)}: {yaml_str('api/' + match['filename'])}")
                else:
                    # Root files: flat (no sub-layer)
                    for mod_name, match in dir_groups[dir_path]:
                        lines.append(f"{pad}  - {yaml_str(mod_name)}: {yaml_str('api/' + match['filename'])}")
        else:
            # All root files → flat list
            for _dir_path, mod_name, match in matched:
                lines.append(f"{pad}  - {yaml_str(mod_name)}: {yaml_str('api/' + match['filename'])}")

    return lines
The helper iterates over each section node, formatting its title and recursively traversing any nested children. For modules mapped to the current section, it extracts the directory path from original_path using os.path.dirname. If any module resides within a non-root subdirectory, it groups those modules into directory sub-levels using bare module names. Modules at the root directory level remain flat, preventing redundant directory nestings.

Example: 

# Sourced from write_mkdocs_output when assembling grouped nav
nav_lines = build_grouped_nav(sections, chapter_files, indent=4)

docs.title: collect_all_modules()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def collect_all_modules(sections: list) -> set:

Description: Recursively traverses an arbitrary section hierarchy tree and aggregates all declared module name strings into a unified set.

Parameters: * sections (list[dict]): Hierarchical section tree containing module assignments and optional children.

Returns: * set: Set of unique module name strings referenced throughout the entire hierarchy.

Raises: * None.

def collect_all_modules(sections: list) -> set:
    """Recursively collect all module names referenced in a sections tree."""
    result = set()
    for section in sections:
        result.update(section.get("modules", []))
        if "children" in section:
            result.update(collect_all_modules(section["children"]))
    return result
The function establishes a base set, updates it with all strings found under section.get("modules", []), and checks for the presence of "children". If child nodes exist, it performs a depth-first traversal by calling itself recursively and merging child module sets into the running result.

Example: 

# Validation step in write_mkdocs_output to find orphan modules:
grouped_modules = collect_all_modules(sections)
ungrouped = [cf["module_name"] for cf in chapter_files if cf["module_name"] not in grouped_modules]

docs.title: build_index_sections()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def build_index_sections(lines: list[str], sections: list, chapter_files: list, level: int = 3) -> None:

Description: Recursively constructs Markdown index documentation lines containing section headings and structured summary tables. Appends generated markdown rows in-place into the provided lines accumulator list.

Parameters: * lines (list[str]): Mutable list of strings representing the lines of docs/api/index.md. * sections (list[dict]): Hierarchical list of section definitions to render. * chapter_files (list[dict]): Reference collection of chapter dictionaries used to resolve filenames, module titles, and descriptions. * level (int, optional): Markdown heading depth (number of # characters) for section titles. Defaults to 3.

Returns: * None: Mutates the lines list in-place.

Raises: * None.

def build_index_sections(lines, sections, chapter_files, level=3):
    """Recursively build index.md sections with module tables."""
    heading = "#" * level
    for section in sections:
        lines.append(f"{heading} {section['name']}")
        lines.append("")
        if section.get("modules"):
            lines.append(f"| {get('UI_TH_CHAPTER')} | {get('UI_TH_DESCRIPTION')} |")
            lines.append("|---------|-------------|")
            for mod_name in section["modules"]:
                match = next((cf for cf in chapter_files if cf["module_name"] == mod_name), None)
                if match:
                    display = mod_name
                    # Use description, but if it's the generic mapper description, extract from content
                    desc = match["description"]
                    if desc.startswith("Internal API reference"):
                        content_lines = match["content"].strip().split("\n")
                        for cl in content_lines:
                            cs = cl.strip()
                            if cs and not cs.startswith(("---", "#", "```", "title:", "sidebar_position:")):
                                desc = cs[:120]
                                break
                    lines.append(f"| [{display}]({match['filename']}) | {desc} |")
            lines.append("")
        for child in section.get("children", []):
            build_index_sections(lines, [child], chapter_files, level + 1)
For each section, the helper appends a Markdown header scaled by level followed by a two-column Markdown table listing chapters and their descriptions. If a chapter contains a generic mapper description (e.g., beginning with "Internal API reference"), the function scans the chapter's raw Markdown content, bypassing YAML frontmatter and code blocks, to extract the first substantive sentence as a preview snippet (truncated to 120 characters). It then recurses through any nested children at level + 1.

Example: 

# In write_mkdocs_output during index construction:
index_lines = ["# API Documentation\n"]
build_index_sections(index_lines, sections, chapter_files, level=2)

docs.title: normalize_chapter_links()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def normalize_chapter_links(chapter_files: list[dict]) -> None:

Description: Deterministically post-processes all chapter markdown bodies, rewriting cross-chapter Markdown links ([text](target.md)) into correct relative paths based on directory nesting depth. Resolves ambiguous filenames, strips external URLs, and updates chapter content in-place.

Parameters: * chapter_files (list[dict]): List of mutable chapter dictionaries containing "filename" and "content".

Returns: * None: Mutates the "content" key of dictionaries within chapter_files in-place.

Raises: * None.

docs.title: Phase 1: Canonical Path Indexing and Basename Disambiguation
docs.text:
# Build lookup: various path forms → canonical filename
    filename_lookup = {}
    ambiguous_basenames = set()
    for cf in chapter_files:
        fname = cf["filename"]  # e.g. "CoreService/AccountingService.cs.md"
        filename_lookup[fname] = fname
        basename = fname.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
        if basename in filename_lookup and filename_lookup[basename] != fname:
            ambiguous_basenames.add(basename)
        else:
            filename_lookup[basename] = fname

    # Remove ambiguous basenames (same name in different dirs)
    for ab in ambiguous_basenames:
        filename_lookup.pop(ab, None)
The first phase compiles a canonical lookup mapping both full relative paths and simple basenames to their canonical chapter filenames. If two or more files share an identical basename across different subdirectories, the basename is marked as ambiguous and purged from the dictionary, preventing inaccurate link rewrites.

docs.title: Phase 2: In-Place Cross-Reference Normalization
docs.text:
link_pattern = re.compile(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)#]+\.md)(#[^)]*)?\)")
    fixed_count = 0

    for cf in chapter_files:
        current_dir = os.path.dirname(cf["filename"])  # e.g. "CoreService"

        def fix_link(match, _dir=current_dir):
            nonlocal fixed_count
            text, target, anchor = match.group(1), match.group(2), match.group(3) or ""
            if target.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
                return match.group(0)
            # Try resolving the target as-is (LLM copied verbatim from index)
            canonical = filename_lookup.get(target)
            if not canonical:
                # Try resolving relative to current dir
                resolved = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(_dir, target)).replace("\\", "/")
                canonical = filename_lookup.get(resolved)
            if canonical:
                correct_rel = os.path.relpath(canonical, _dir).replace("\\", "/") if _dir else canonical
                if correct_rel != target:
                    fixed_count += 1
                return f"[{text}]({correct_rel}{anchor})"
            return match.group(0)  # Unknown target — leave as-is

        cf["content"] = link_pattern.sub(fix_link, cf["content"])

    if fixed_count:
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"LINK NORMALIZATION | fixed {fixed_count} cross-chapter links", dest="LOG")
This phase scans each chapter's content with regular expression r"\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)#]+\.md)(#[^)]*)?\)". For every non-HTTP target, it attempts to resolve the path directly against filename_lookup or relative to the source chapter's directory via os.path.normpath. If a matching canonical file is found, os.path.relpath calculates the exact relative path required to navigate between directories, rewriting the link target while preserving any fragment #anchor.

Example: 

# Direct normalization invocation inside write_mkdocs_output:
normalize_chapter_links(chapter_files)

Visibility: Private Signature: def build_mermaid_init_js() -> str:

Description: Returns the raw JavaScript source code required to initialize client-side Mermaid diagram rendering within Material for MkDocs.

Returns: * str: Raw JavaScript contents defined by MERMAID_INIT_JS.

This helper exposes the module-level constant string MERMAID_INIT_JS to client asset writers. The script registers an event listener on DOMContentLoaded that unwraps diagram text from <pre class="mermaid-raw"><code> blocks into raw <pre class="mermaid-raw"> containers before invoking mermaid.run(), ensuring correct parsing and rendering behavior.

Example:

docs.title: MERMAID_INIT_JS
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Type: str

Description: Module-level JavaScript snippet embedded into output sites. Configures Mermaid 11 client runtime settings (theme: 'default', securityLevel: 'loose') and unwraps <pre class="mermaid-raw"><code> code blocks produced by PyMdown Extensions superfences.

// Mermaid initialization for MkDocs Material.
//
// Material for MkDocs targets .mermaid class for its own color overrides.
// By using .mermaid-raw, diagrams render with Mermaid's default theme:
// yellow subgraph backgrounds, lavender nodes, clean rectangles.
//
// pymdownx.superfences fence_code_format wraps content as:
//   <pre class="mermaid-raw"><code>flowchart TD ...</code></pre>
// Mermaid expects the diagram text directly in the target element,
// so we unwrap the <code> child before calling mermaid.run().
(function() {
  function initMermaid() {
    if (typeof mermaid === 'undefined') return;
    try {
      // Unwrap: move <code> text content up to <pre> and remove <code>
      document.querySelectorAll('pre.mermaid-raw > code').forEach(function(code) {
        var pre = code.parentElement;
        pre.textContent = code.textContent;
      });
      mermaid.initialize({
        startOnLoad: false,
        theme: 'default',
        securityLevel: 'loose'
      });
      mermaid.run({ querySelector: '.mermaid-raw' }).catch(function(err) {
        console.warn('Mermaid render error:', err);
      });
    } catch (e) {
      console.warn('Mermaid init error:', e);
    }
  }
  if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', initMermaid);
  } else {
    initMermaid();
  }
})();

docs.title: LLM Grouping Failure and Degradation
docs.text:
During navigation grouping in write_mkdocs_output(), prompt execution or YAML decoding may fail due to schema mismatches, network refusals, or rate limits. The module protects the pipeline via defensive exception handling:

        except Exception as e:
            emit("GROUP_ERROR_FALLBACK", error=e)
            emit_raw("ERROR", f"LLM grouping failed: {e}\n{traceback.format_exc()}", dest="LOG")
            nav_snippet = prep_res["nav_snippet"]
            sections = None
When an exception occurs, the error is recorded, an event notification is emitted via emit("GROUP_ERROR_FALLBACK"), and the navigation tree falls back to the deterministic flat prep_res["nav_snippet"].

docs.title: Orphaned Module Recovery
docs.text:
When an LLM generates section assignments, it may inadvertently omit modules present in chapter_files. To prevent unreferenced documentation files:

        if sections:
            grouped_modules = collect_all_modules(sections)
            ungrouped = [cf["module_name"] for cf in chapter_files if cf["module_name"] not in grouped_modules]
            if ungrouped:
                sections.append({"name": get("UI_OTHER"), "modules": ungrouped})
The set difference isolates unassigned modules and dynamically creates an "Other" section (get("UI_OTHER")), ensuring all compiled files remain accessible through the navigation tree.

docs.title: Ambiguous Basename Collision Resolution
docs.text:
During cross-chapter link normalization, multiple source files located in different directories may share the same filename (for example, models/user.py.md and api/user.py.md). If a link references only user.py.md, rewriting could result in an invalid relative link. To prevent incorrect rewrites:

    for cf in chapter_files:
        fname = cf["filename"]
        filename_lookup[fname] = fname
        basename = fname.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
        if basename in filename_lookup and filename_lookup[basename] != fname:
            ambiguous_basenames.add(basename)
        else:
            filename_lookup[basename] = fname

    for ab in ambiguous_basenames:
        filename_lookup.pop(ab, None)
Duplicate basenames are detected, flagged, and removed from the fallback resolution dictionary, ensuring only unambiguous references are rewritten.

docs.title: output.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/output.py

Following the generation and layout assembly handled by mkdocs.py, the utils/output.py module serves as the centralized terminal presentation, telemetry broadcasting, and persistent file logging engine for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. It decouples hardcoded console output and operational notifications from core pipeline logic, routing all human-facing messaging through a structured, multi-lingual localization catalog.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/output.py implements a unified, level-aware messaging bus designed to handle simultaneous standard output rendering and persistent file-based audit logging. The architecture abstracts string presentation behind symbolic keys defined in an external CSV catalog (utils/strings.csv). By standardizing user messages around unique identifier keys, the system supports dynamic multi-language localization, safe variable interpolation, and centralized level styling without scattering formatting logic across workflow nodes or low-level transport adapters.

A critical design challenge addressed by the module is managing output during early runtime initialization—specifically before command-line parsing, project directory creation, or log file configuration occurs. Standard library logging systems often drop early telemetry or require complex early-handler setups. utils/output.py solves this by introducing a bounded in-memory buffer (_pending_log) that holds preflight entries (such as credential checks, environment verification, and auto-translation records). Once configure_logging() executes, the buffered messages are atomically flushed into the newly initialized run log, ensuring continuous audit trails without data loss.

The module also handles cross-platform encoding constraints and console routing rules. On non-interactive or redirected standard output streams (notably on Windows environments where non-UTF-8 code pages like CP-1252 would trigger UnicodeEncodeError when printing localized CJK or accented Latin text), the module safely reconfigures stdout and stderr streams to UTF-8. Message routing supports multiple destination targets (BOTH, STDOUT, LOG, and debug-gated variants DBOTH, DSTDOUT), pairing ANSI terminal color sequences with unadorned, ISO-8601-timestamped file logs.

flowchart TD
    initNode["Initialize output system: init()"] --> streamCheck["Reconfigure non-TTY streams to UTF-8"]
    streamCheck --> loadCSV["Load strings.csv into memory"]
    loadCSV --> autoTransCheck{"auto_translate flag active?"}
    autoTransCheck -- Yes --> runAutoTrans["Invoke i18n.auto_translate()"]
    autoTransCheck -- No --> callerLoop["Caller invokes emit(), emit_raw(), or get()"]
    runAutoTrans --> callerLoop

    subgraph SubgraphRouting["Message Routing Engine"]
        routeStart["Evaluate destination: BOTH, STDOUT, LOG, DBOTH, DSTDOUT"]
        routeStart --> debugCheck{"Is destination D-prefixed?"}
        debugCheck -- Yes, debug active --> stripDPrefix["Strip prefix: DBOTH to BOTH, DSTDOUT to STDOUT"]
        debugCheck -- Yes, debug inactive --> divertToLog["Set destination to LOG only"]
        debugCheck -- No --> evaluateDest{"Target destination?"}
        stripDPrefix --> evaluateDest
        divertToLog --> evaluateDest
        evaluateDest -- STDOUT or BOTH --> renderTerminal["Apply ANSI color code and print to terminal"]
        evaluateDest -- LOG or BOTH --> writeBuffer["Pass to _write_log()"]
    end

    subgraph SubgraphLogging["File Logging Pipeline"]
        logStart["_write_log(level, text)"]
        logStart --> handleCheck{"Is _log_file initialized?"}
        handleCheck -- No --> bufferQueue["Append to _pending_log (capped at 5,000 lines)"]
        handleCheck -- Yes --> flushFile["Format timestamp: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,fff"]
        flushFile --> writeDisk["Write line to disk and flush"]
    end

    callerLoop --> routeStart
    writeBuffer --> logStart

docs.title: init()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def init(language="english", use_cache=True, thinking_level=None, debug=False, auto_translate=True) -> None

Description: Initializes the output subsystem by setting module-level configuration state, ensuring UTF-8 stream compliance across operating system pipes, loading the localization database from strings.csv, and optionally triggering large language model auto-translation for missing localization tokens. Must be invoked from the application entry point (main()) before invoking any messaging helpers.

Parameters: * language (str): Target localization language name (e.g., "english", "vietnamese"). Defaults to "english". * use_cache (bool): Flag indicating whether downstream LLM translation calls should leverage response caching. Defaults to True. * thinking_level (Any): Configured reasoning/thinking effort level forwarded to downstream LLM translation invocations. Defaults to None. * debug (bool): Global switch enabling verbose diagnostic outputs and activating DBOTH / DSTDOUT console routing targets. Defaults to False. * auto_translate (bool): If True, synchronously scans and translates missing string catalog entries during initialization. When False, defers translation until credentials and arguments are validated. Defaults to True.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised directly; failures during string loading or translation degrade gracefully to English fallback values.

Example: 

# Extracted from utils/output.py initialization usage:
init(
    language="vietnamese",
    use_cache=True,
    thinking_level=None,
    debug=False,
    auto_translate=False,
)


def init(language="english", use_cache=True, thinking_level=None, debug=False, auto_translate=True):
    global _language, _lang_col, _csv_path, _use_cache, _thinking_level, _debug
    _language = language.capitalize()
    _lang_col = language.lower()
    _csv_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "strings.csv")
    _use_cache = use_cache
    _thinking_level = thinking_level
    _debug = debug
    _ensure_utf8_streams()
    _load_strings()
    if auto_translate:
        _auto_translate()
The init() function establishes the runtime state required for all subsequent output operations across the system. It canonicalizes the language parameters by generating a capitalized display representation (_language) alongside a normalized lowercase column key (_lang_col) matching CSV schema headers. It then dynamically anchors the catalog path to utils/strings.csv using the file's directory path. Stream sanity checks (_ensure_utf8_streams) and catalog parsing (_load_strings) are executed immediately. If auto_translate is enabled, the helper immediately attempts to resolve missing localization definitions via downstream LLM integration.

docs.title: translate_missing_strings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def translate_missing_strings() -> None

Description: Public entry point to trigger the automated translation of missing string entries in strings.csv using the configured target language and LLM provider. Used when init() was called with auto_translate=False to defer model inference until CLI arguments and LLM authentication keys have passed validation checks.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised directly.

Example: 

# Defers translation until authentication preflight succeeds
init(language="vietnamese", auto_translate=False)
# ... validate CLI flags and LLM credentials ...
translate_missing_strings()


def translate_missing_strings():
    """Auto-translate strings missing for the configured language (LLM call); see init(auto_translate=False)."""
    _auto_translate()
This utility acts as a clean public wrapper delegating execution to the internal _auto_translate() helper. It enables the primary application workflow in main.py to decouple output subsystem initialization from active network calls. Because language model translation relies on verified credentials and established provider endpoints, postponing catalog translation guarantees that missing keys will not trigger premature network exceptions before authentication preflights conclude.

docs.title: emit()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def emit(key: str, suffix: str = "", **kwargs) -> None

Description: Retrieves a translatable template string from the in-memory catalog using a symbolic key, interpolates keyword variables safely, appends an optional unformatted suffix, and directs the resulting message to terminal standard output and/or the run log file according to catalog destination rules and debug switches.

Parameters: * key (str): Identifier key matching an entry in strings.csv (e.g., "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER"). * suffix (str): Optional string appended directly to the end of the formatted message (e.g., raw token counts or duration statistics). Defaults to "". * **kwargs: Key-value pairs for string template interpolation via Python .format() substitution.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised. If key is missing from strings.csv, prints an [UNKNOWN STRING: {key}] warning directly to standard output.

Example: 

# Emit a localized progress message with dynamic parameters and token breakdown
emit("LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER", suffix=" [1,420 tokens]", chapter_num=1, name="flow")


def emit(key, suffix="", **kwargs):
    entry = _strings.get(key)
    if not entry:
        # Fallback for unknown keys — print raw so nothing is silently lost
        print(f"[UNKNOWN STRING: {key}]")
        return

    text = _format_safe(entry["text"], kwargs)
    if suffix:
        text = text + suffix

    level = entry["level"]
    dest = entry["dest"]

    # D-prefixed destinations (DBOTH, DSTDOUT): debug-gated console output.
    # Without --debug, suppress console but always log. Preserves original color from LEVEL.
    if dest.startswith("D"):
        if _debug:
            dest = dest[1:]  # DBOTH → BOTH, DSTDOUT → STDOUT
        else:
            dest = "LOG"

    color = COLORS.get(level, "")
    reset = RESET if color else ""

    if dest in ("BOTH", "STDOUT"):
        print(f"{color}{text}{reset}")
    if dest in ("BOTH", "LOG"):
        _write_log(level, text)
The emit() function serves as the standard emission interface for all cataloged pipeline events. When invoked, it looks up the key in the module's _strings cache and passes the raw template along with kwargs to _format_safe(). If a routing destination begins with D (such as DBOTH or DSTDOUT), it checks the active _debug state: if debug mode is active, the prefix is stripped to allow console printing; otherwise, the destination is demoted to LOG to keep console output clean while preserving audit history. Terminal output applies ANSI color sequences mapped to the entry's level (COLORS.get(level)), while file logging via _write_log() records the plain message tagged with the uncolored level name.

docs.title: emit_raw()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def emit_raw(level: str, text: str, dest: str = "BOTH") -> None

Description: Emits a pre-formatted string directly to console and/or file destinations without referencing strings.csv. Designed for dynamic structural outputs, diagnostic banners, tables, and un-templatized operational details.

Parameters: * level (str): Log level determining ANSI terminal coloration ("PROGRESS", "SUCCESS", "WARNING", "ERROR", "INFO", "DEBUG", "FILE_WRITE", or "UI"). * text (str): Pre-formatted text payload to display and log. * dest (str): Output destination routing target ("BOTH", "STDOUT", or "LOG"). Defaults to "BOTH".

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Output a dynamic crawl summary table directly to both console and log file
emit_raw("SUCCESS", "Crawled 142 local files successfully (8.4 MB total)", dest="BOTH")


def emit_raw(level, text, dest="BOTH"):
    # DEBUG-level: suppress console unless --debug is active
    if level == "DEBUG" and not _debug:
        dest = "LOG"

    color = COLORS.get(level, "")
    reset = RESET if color else ""

    if dest in ("BOTH", "STDOUT"):
        print(f"{color}{text}{reset}")
    if dest in ("BOTH", "LOG"):
        _write_log(level, text)
emit_raw() bypasses catalog lookups entirely to accommodate dynamic runtime data, such as ASCII trees, table formatting, or batch processing summaries. If the supplied level is set to "DEBUG" and global debug mode is disabled, the function diverts the destination to "LOG". This ensures verbose debugging diagnostics are persistently captured in the run log without cluttering standard output. ANSI color formatting and destination routing follow the exact same mechanics as emit().

docs.title: is_debug()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def is_debug() -> bool

Description: Queries the module's internal debug status flag. Used by external components to conditionally construct expensive debug messages or gate verbose diagnostic collections.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * bool: True if --debug mode is enabled; False otherwise.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Gate expensive token layout calculation behind debug check
if is_debug():
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"Tiktoken breakdown: {detailed_token_map}")


def is_debug():
    """Return True when --debug is active (used to gate verbose diagnostics outside this module)."""
    return _debug
This query helper allows calling modules to inspect the active debugging state without directly mutating or accessing private module-level state variables. It prevents upstream callers from incurring formatting overhead—such as generating serialized JSON payloads or inspecting large data structures—when debug output is suppressed.

docs.title: get()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get(key: str, **kwargs) -> str

Description: Retrieves a translated string template for a given key, performs variable substitution with supplied keyword arguments, and returns the raw string without printing or logging. Primarily utilized to obtain localized headings, section titles, and interface labels embedded inside generated Markdown documents.

Parameters: * key (str): Catalog key identifier defined in strings.csv. * **kwargs: Key-value pairs for template variable interpolation.

Returns: * str: The localized, interpolated string. If the key is not found in the catalog, returns key as a fallback.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Retrieve localized section header for MkDocs index generation
section_title = get("UI_MODULE_OVERVIEW", module_name="Authentication")


def get(key, **kwargs):
    entry = _strings.get(key)
    if not entry:
        return key  # Fallback: return the key itself
    return _format_safe(entry["text"], kwargs)
get() exposes the localization engine directly to document-generation modules like mkdocs.py. Unlike emit(), it does not write to standard output or persist lines to _log_file. If a key is absent from the in-memory cache, it safely degrades by returning the raw key identifier, preventing template generation pipelines from failing due to missing UI strings.

docs.title: configure_logging()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def configure_logging(project_name: str = "project", mode: str = "tutorial") -> str

Description: Configures and opens a dedicated, timestamped file log on disk. Flushes any log entries accumulated in the in-memory buffer (_pending_log) prior to configuration and prints initial execution metadata headers.

Parameters: * project_name (str): Name of the target project or repository being analyzed. Sanitized for filesystem safety. Defaults to "project". * mode (str): Operating pipeline mode (e.g., "tutorial", "api-reference"). Defaults to "tutorial".

Returns: * str: Absolute or relative path to the newly created log file.

Raises: * OSError: If log directory creation or file handle allocation fails due to filesystem permissions.

Example: 

# Initialize disk logging for a project workflow run
log_filepath = configure_logging(project_name="my_repo", mode="api-reference")
# Output: logs/my_repo_api_reference_20260330_141500.log


def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial"):
    global _log_file

    log_directory = os.getenv("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    os.makedirs(log_directory, exist_ok=True)

    safe_project = "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in project_name)
    safe_mode = mode.replace("-", "_")
    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    log_path = os.path.join(log_directory, f"{safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{timestamp}.log")

    # Close any existing log file
    if _log_file is not None:
        _log_file.close()

    _log_file = open(log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8")  # noqa: SIM115

    # Log run metadata at the start of every log file
    sep = "=" * 80
    emit_raw("INFO", sep, dest="LOG")
    emit_raw("INFO", f"RUN STARTED | project={project_name} | mode={mode} | timestamp={timestamp}", dest="LOG")
    emit_raw("INFO", f"Log file: {log_path}", dest="LOG")
    if _pending_log:
        _log_file.write("".join(_pending_log))
        _log_file.flush()
        _pending_log.clear()

    return log_path
configure_logging() manages log file creation and initialization for each run. It resolves the output directory from the LOG_DIR environment variable (defaulting to logs/) and creates it if necessary using os.makedirs. Project names and modes are sanitized to alphanumeric and safe delimiter characters (-_) to prevent path traversal or filesystem errors. Any previously open file handle assigned to _log_file is closed. It then opens the target path in append mode with explicit utf-8 encoding. Initial metadata headers are logged, and all buffered log messages stored in _pending_log are written to disk and flushed before clearing the memory buffer.

docs.title: shutdown()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def shutdown() -> None

Description: Closes the open log file handle and releases associated filesystem resources. Should be executed within the finally block of the top-level application entry point to ensure all buffered entries are committed to disk.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Ensure clean resource release upon application exit
try:
    run_pipeline()
finally:
    shutdown()


def shutdown():
    """Close the log file handle and release resources.

    Should be called at the end of main() in a finally block to ensure
    the log file is properly flushed and closed.
    """
    global _log_file
    if _log_file is not None:
        _log_file.close()
        _log_file = None
shutdown() guarantees that the active log file descriptor is properly flushed and closed upon system termination. It safely inspects _log_file, invokes .close(), and resets the reference to None. This prevents file locking issues or truncated trailing logs across repeated runs or automated test suites.

docs.title: _write_log()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _write_log(level: str, text: str) -> None

Description: Internal logging worker that formats a single log entry with a microsecond-precision timestamp and level marker. If configure_logging() has not yet been executed, the entry is queued in _pending_log (bounded to PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES). Once configured, entries are written directly to _log_file and flushed.

Parameters: * level (str): Log level category identifier (e.g., "PROGRESS", "ERROR", "INFO"). * text (str): Uncolored text payload of the message.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Internal invocation from emit() or emit_raw()
_write_log("INFO", "Discovered 42 files matching inclusion criteria")


def _write_log(level, text):
    """Write a timestamped line to the log file (buffered until configure_logging opens it)."""
    ts = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S,%f")[:-3]
    line = f"{ts} - {level} - {text}\n"
    if _log_file is None:
        _pending_log.append(line)
        if len(_pending_log) > PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES:
            del _pending_log[0]
        return
    _log_file.write(line)
    _log_file.flush()
_write_log() handles log record serialization. Timestamps are formatted as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,fff by truncating microsecond measurements to milliseconds. When _log_file is None, entries are appended to the _pending_log list. To prevent memory leaks during long-running workflows that do not configure logging, the list is capped at PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES (5,000) using a FIFO eviction pattern (del _pending_log[0]). When the file is active, lines are immediately written and flushed to guarantee real-time log persistence.

docs.title: _ensure_utf8_streams()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _ensure_utf8_streams() -> None

Description: Inspects sys.stdout and sys.stderr to identify non-interactive, redirected, or piped execution environments, reconfiguring their output encodings to utf-8 when necessary.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Executed automatically during init()
_ensure_utf8_streams()


def _ensure_utf8_streams():
    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
        encoding = (getattr(stream, "encoding", "") or "").lower().replace("-", "")
        if hasattr(stream, "reconfigure") and encoding != "utf8" and not stream.isatty():
            stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
This utility prevents encoding crashes on Windows platforms when output is piped to another process or redirected to a file. Interactive consoles on modern Python runtimes (PEP 528) use UTF-8 by default, but redirected streams often fall back to legacy system codepages like CP-1252. If a non-TTY stream does not use UTF-8, _ensure_utf8_streams() invokes stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"). This ensures Unicode characters (such as CJK text or accented characters) can be safely output without raising UnicodeEncodeError.

docs.title: _format_safe()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _format_safe(template: str, kwargs: dict) -> str

Description: Safely interpolates keyword variables into a template string using template.format(**kwargs), gracefully suppressing formatting errors if keys are missing or malformed.

Parameters: * template (str): Template string containing {placeholder} tokens. * kwargs (dict): Dictionary of keyword arguments to interpolate into the template.

Returns: * str: The formatted string, or the original unaltered template if an interpolation error occurs.

Raises: * No exceptions raised; catches KeyError, IndexError, and ValueError.

Example: 

# Safely handles missing template variables without throwing exceptions
formatted = _format_safe("Processing {current} of {total}", {"current": 5})
# Returns "Processing {current} of {total}" if 'total' is missing


def _format_safe(template, kwargs):
    """Apply .format(**kwargs) with graceful fallback on missing keys."""
    try:
        return template.format(**kwargs)
    except (KeyError, IndexError, ValueError):
        return template
_format_safe() provides error isolation for string formatting. Dynamic templates loaded from strings.csv can contain placeholder variables (e.g., {project}, {count}). If caller invocations omit an expected keyword argument or the template contains unbalanced braces, standard .format() raises KeyError, IndexError, or ValueError. This helper traps those exceptions and returns the raw template string as a fallback, ensuring that messaging errors never interrupt core pipeline processing.

docs.title: _load_strings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _load_strings() -> None

Description: Parses utils/strings.csv using csv.DictReader and populates the internal _strings catalog dictionary. Implements localized fallback resolution, defaulting to English values if the target language column entry is missing or empty.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * OSError: If the CSV file is inaccessible due to invalid permissions (file existence is checked prior to reading).

Example: 

# Reload the internal string cache after file modifications
_load_strings()


def _load_strings():
    global _strings
    _strings = {}

    if not _csv_path or not os.path.exists(_csv_path):
        return

    translated_count = 0
    total_count = 0

    with open(_csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if not key or key.startswith("#"):
                continue

            level = row.get("LEVEL", "INFO").strip()
            dest = row.get("DEST", "BOTH").strip()

            # Priority: language column → English fallback
            text = row.get(_lang_col, "").strip()
            if text:
                translated_count += 1
            else:
                text = row.get("english", "").strip()

            total_count += 1
            _strings[key] = {"text": text, "level": level, "dest": dest}

    if _lang_col != "english" and translated_count == total_count:
        emit_raw("SUCCESS", f"[i18n] {_language} — loaded {translated_count} strings from CSV")
_load_strings() initializes and populates the in-memory string catalog. It opens _csv_path using utf-8-sig encoding to transparently strip any Byte Order Marks (BOM) introduced by text editors or Microsoft Excel. It iterates through each row, skipping blank lines and comment rows starting with #. For each valid key, it checks the configured language column (_lang_col); if empty, it falls back to the "english" column. Entries are stored in _strings as dictionaries containing "text", "level", and "dest". If a non-English language is fully translated, a success notification is emitted.

docs.title: _auto_translate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _auto_translate() -> None

Description: Lazily imports utils.i18n.auto_translate to translate any missing string entries in strings.csv for the configured language, subsequently reloading the cache via _load_strings() if new translations were written.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * Traps errors downstream; does not propagate translation exceptions.

Example: 

# Internal invocation triggered by init() or translate_missing_strings()
_auto_translate()


def _auto_translate():
    """Auto-translate missing strings via LLM and write back into strings.csv."""
    from utils.i18n import auto_translate

    if auto_translate(_lang_col, _language, _csv_path, _use_cache, _thinking_level):
        # Reload strings from the updated CSV so all translations are active
        _load_strings()
_auto_translate() integrates localization updates into the output module. To prevent circular import cycles between output.py, i18n.py, and call_llm.py, auto_translate is imported dynamically inside the function body. If auto_translate() returns True (indicating that new translations were generated and persisted to the CSV file), _auto_translate() calls _load_strings() to refresh the in-memory cache so subsequent emit() calls use the updated translations.

docs.title: ANSI Color Palette (COLORS)
docs.text:
Mapping of semantic output levels to their corresponding ANSI escape sequences:

Level Key ANSI Escape Code Rendered Appearance Intended Context "PROGRESS" "\033[96m" Cyan LLM invocations, active pipeline steps, crawl loops "SUCCESS" "\033[92m" Green Successful step completions, cache hits, finish notices "WARNING" "\033[93m" Yellow Non-fatal alerts, context window limits, fallbacks "ERROR" "\033[91m" Red Fatal failures, API rejections, unhandled exceptions "INFO" "" Standard Console Configuration parameters, file counts, telemetry headers "DEBUG" "\033[90m" Gray Ignored paths, fine-grained AST parsing, debug logs "FILE_WRITE" "" Standard Console File serialization logs (- Wrote {path}) "UI" "" Standard Console Markdown headers and UI labels (never styled)

docs.title: Module State Registry
docs.text:
The module maintains runtime state across multiple module-level variables:

Variable Type Default Value Description _strings dict[str, dict[str, str]] {} In-memory cache mapping string keys to their configuration dictionaries. _language str "English" Capitalized display name of active localization language. _lang_col str "english" Lowercase column header used for CSV lookups. _log_file io.TextIOWrapper or None None Open file handle pointing to the active log file on disk. _pending_log list[str] [] FIFO queue holding log entries generated before log file initialization. PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES int 5000 Maximum capacity of _pending_log before dropping the oldest entries. _csv_path str or None None Absolute filesystem path resolving to utils/strings.csv. _use_cache bool True Global flag indicating if translation LLM calls should use caching. _thinking_level Any None Reasoning effort level passed to translation LLM calls. _debug bool False Global flag controlling verbose debug output and destination routing.

docs.title: Internal String Record (_strings Entry Schema)
docs.text:
Shape of the dictionary stored for each entry in the _strings map:

Field Type Description text str Localized string template containing optional {placeholder} markers. level str Semantic level name corresponding to a key in the COLORS table. dest str Routing destination determining terminal and/or log file output. 
# Example structure of an entry in _strings
{
    "text": "Call LLM: writing chapter {chapter_num} ({name})",
    "level": "PROGRESS",
    "dest": "BOTH",
}

docs.title: Destination Routing Targets
docs.text:
Supported destination values configured in strings.csv or passed to emit_raw():

Target Identifier Terminal Visibility File Log Visibility Debug Gated? Notes "BOTH" Yes Yes No Standard operational notifications. "STDOUT" Yes No No Interactive notices that should bypass log files. "LOG" No Yes No Verbose telemetry and raw diagnostic traces. "DBOTH" Conditional Yes Yes Diverts to LOG unless --debug is active. "DSTDOUT" Conditional No Yes Suppressed completely unless --debug is active. "UI" No No No Never emitted directly; accessed via get().

docs.title: Non-Interactive Stream Transcoding
docs.text: On Windows platforms, redirected standard output streams often default to legacy single-byte codepages (e.g., CP-1252), causing UnicodeEncodeError when non-ASCII characters are encountered. The module resolves this by checking stream.isatty() in _ensure_utf8_streams() and reconfiguring non-TTY streams using stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"). This ensures Unicode strings are safely output without raising encoding exceptions.

docs.title: Safe Template Variable Substitution
docs.text:
Templates loaded from strings.csv rely on bracketed placeholders (e.g., {project_name}). The internal helper _format_safe() intercepts formatting exceptions: 

try:
    return template.format(**kwargs)
except (KeyError, IndexError, ValueError):
    return template
If caller invocations omit required parameters or include mismatched types, the exception is caught and the original template string is returned as a fallback. This guarantees that missing formatting variables do not cause runtime failures during output emission.

docs.title: Missing Key and Unknown Entry Fallbacks
docs.text: If an unrecognized key is passed to emit() or get(), the module falls back gracefully instead of raising exceptions: * emit() prints a raw warning: [UNKNOWN STRING: {key}]. * get() returns the raw key string, allowing document generation pipelines to continue without interruptions from missing UI labels.

docs.title: Bounded In-Memory Buffering
docs.text: Log entries generated before log file initialization are held in _pending_log. To prevent unbounded memory consumption during long-running workflows without file logging, the buffer is capped at 5,000 lines (PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES). Once this threshold is reached, older entries are dropped using a FIFO queue strategy (del _pending_log[0]).

docs.title: prompts.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/prompts.py

Following the console logging, terminal styling, and localized string management provided by output.py, the prompts.py module encapsulates prompt loading, inline prompt generation, and model response extraction. It decouples the synthesis pipeline's prompt lifecycle from model invocation drivers, providing unified filesystem loaders for Markdown prompt templates and robust parsing routines for model-generated YAML data structures and file indices.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The prompts.py module provides centralized prompt construction and response parsing utilities across the repository documentation pipeline. Upstream workflow graph nodes in nodes.py require structured communication with Large Language Models (LLMs) across multiple operational modes, including tutorial, advanced, api-reference, and sdk. This module abstracts prompt template locations on disk, ensures safe UTF-8 file reading with Byte Order Mark handling, dynamically generates specialized inline prompts, and extracts structured data from LLM text completions.

A critical design requirement of the response parsing layer is defense against silent failure modes caused by LLM output truncation. When model completions hit max token ceilings, partial YAML blocks can sometimes be parsed as incomplete data structures (such as truncated lists or dictionaries), leading to silently dropped files or corrupted chapter structures. The module prevents this by validating response objects for truncation sentinels (such as TruncatedResponse defined in llm_common.py) prior to YAML parsing, failing fast with explicit exceptions that prompt workflow nodes to retry.
